item.title: NCP strongly condemns attack on Badhon in Venice
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has strongly condemned the attack on actress and cultural activist Azmeri Haque Badhon in Venice, Italy, expressing “deep anger” over the incident and blaming local leaders and activists of the banned Awami League.
NCP Convener Nahid Islam and Member Secretary Akhtar Hossain made the remarks in a joint statement sent to the media on Tuesday.
The party condemned the alleged physical assault on Badhon and attacks on the women and children accompanying her, saying the incident demonstrated that the mentality of violence associated with the Awami League had not changed.
The NCP leaders alleged that activists of the Awami League, which they described as a “fascist” organisation, were continuing political violence against July uprising activists from abroad.
They claimed that identified Awami League activists in Venice attacked Badhon and her family and forced her to chant slogans including “Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu”.
According to the NCP, photographs of some of those involved with Sajeeb Wazed Joy had circulated on social media. The party alleged that the attack was carried out with the support or encouragement of senior Awami League leaders living abroad.
The NCP called on the relevant authorities in Italy to arrest those involved, cancel their visas and deport them to Bangladesh so that they can face legal action.
The party also urged Bangladesh’s diplomatic missions to take effective measures to ensure the safety of July uprising activists, expatriate activists and Bangladeshi citizens abroad.
The NCP said no political or social reconciliation was possible with what it described as the “fascist group”, arguing that the alleged attack in Venice was further evidence of continued political violence beyond Bangladesh’s borders.
“July warriors who brought down the dictatorship are national assets. The audacity shown by the cadres of this terrorist organisation in attacking them on foreign soil will not be tolerated under any circumstances,” the statement said.
Nahid and Akhtar warned that the government would have to take a strong position if those involved in the Venice attack were not brought to justice through diplomatic and legal channels.
They said the NCP, together with the people of Bangladesh, would resist what it described as allies of “fascism” on domestic and international platforms.

item.title: North Korea calls Russia bridge a sign of tighter ties
item.description:
North Korea called the first road bridge across its narrow border with Russia a concrete sign of tightening bonds, state media reported Tuesday, as Pyongyang gains advantages from its powerful neighbors Moscow and Beijing.
The bridge over the Tumen River into Russia and an under-construction span to China are part of a shift that offers Western-sanctioned Pyongyang economic and strategic options it has long sought, experts said.
North Korea “will simultaneously secure two major overland routes linking it with Russia and China, allowing it to encourage competition between the two countries and maximize its gains,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University.
He noted the bridges also “can be a message to the United States that North Korea has no reason to beg Washington for sanctions relief or make concessions on denuclearization in order to negotiate.”
Russia noted the bridge is designed to accommodate expanded growth in freight with the capacity for up to 300 vehicles daily, which adds to the rail and air links already between the neighbors.
Ukrainian rights group Truth Hounds, however, previously warned that the new bridge could become “a direct artery for moving North Korean troops, construction brigades and military officials into Russia, with Russian technology and resources flowing in the opposite direction.”
The ceremony on Monday marking the new bridge’s opening came as Russia and North Korea have heavily boosted military and economic ties since Moscow launched its Ukraine offensive in 2022.
North Korea dispatched thousands of troops to Russia in 2024 to help ward off a Ukrainian incursion into the Kursk region, while Kyiv has accused Moscow of using North Korean missiles in its regular barrages.
South Korea’s central bank estimated in July that North Korea’s economy grew more than three percent for a third straight year in 2025, citing its expansion of economic cooperation with Russia as a “major drive.”
The bank’s official said North Korea’s gross national income also “received a boost from a sharp rise in foreign currency earnings” linked to the deployment of its troops to Russia.
North Korean official Pak Thae Song, according the official Kcna news agency, said “the completion of the bridge is a significant event adding a new dynamic movement to the overall bilateral cooperation.”
North Korea and China are already connected by the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which is regularly used by passenger trains, but its capacity is limited.
After a long halt, the bridge partly reopened and restored daily passenger train services with China early this year, but has not yet resumed issuing tourism visas to Chinese citizens, who once made up the bulk of its overseas visitors.
North Korea has long kept tight control over foreign visitors, and effectively sealed its borders at the start of the pandemic six years ago.
The New Yalu River Bridge, intended as an alternative and eventual replacement of the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, is expected by experts to be completed this year.
The completion of the bridge “sends a political and geopolitical message demonstrating the formation of a “North Korea-China-Russia continental triangular bloc,” said Lim.

Rail communication with Dhaka resumes after bogie derails in Santahar
item.description:
Rail communication between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh resumed nearly four and a half hours after a bogie of the Dhaka-bound Kurigram Express derailed at Santahar Railway Station in Bogra on Monday.
The incident occurred at around 6:30pm when the train, travelling from Kurigram to Dhaka, reached the rail gate area of Santahar Junction Station. A freight bogie at the rear of the train derailed, disrupting rail communication between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh.
Santahar Station Master Khadija Khanam and Santahar Railway Police Station OC Dulal Uddin confirmed the incident.
No passengers were injured in the derailment.
A railway rescue team began work immediately after the incident. At around 10pm, the derailed bogie was separated from the train, allowing the remaining coaches to continue towards Dhaka.
A relief train reached the site at around 10:30pm. After about an hour of work, the derailed bogie was removed from the tracks and the damaged railway line was repaired.
Train movement on the northern route resumed at around 11:30pm after railway officials declared the line safe.
The derailment caused significant disruption for passengers and local residents.
Abdul Aziz, a passenger on the Kurigram Express, said the train was already running five to six hours late before the derailment.
“Even then, we had to wait for at least another four and a half hours after the derailment. All the passengers suffered because of this,” he said.
Local resident Parvez Pramanik said the derailment near the rail gate halted movement between the two sides of the area for a long time, causing severe traffic congestion.
Station Master Khadija Khanam said the freight bogie at the rear of the train had derailed. The damaged bogie was detached and kept separate while the remaining train was moved to platform No 3 before departing for Dhaka.
She said an investigation committee would be formed to determine the cause of the derailment.

item.title: Zverev romps into quarter-finals as Darderi downed
item.description:
Top seed Alexander Zverev romped into the quarter-finals of the US Open on Monday with a straight sets defeat of Italy's Luciano Darderi.
Zverev, who had been taken to five sets in his opening two matches of the tournament, raced past 21st seed Darderi 6-2, 6-2, 7-6 (7/3) in 2hr 30mins on the Arthur Ashe Stadium court.
The 29-year-old French Open champion was in complete control throughout, punishing Darderi's woeful service game to grab an early double break in the first set for a 3-0 lead.
Darderi, who has failed to go further than the fourth round at any Grand Slam in his career, never looked like forcing his way back into the set thereafter.
Zverev mopped up the first set easily and was soon back on the attack in the second, once again securing a quick double-break for a 3-0 lead before holding with ease to go two sets up.
Darderi did manage to rally in the third set, suddenly finding his range with some blistering forehands and holding off four break points in the 11th game to help set up a tie-break.
But Zverev's superior service game meant there was only going to be one winner in the tie-break, a thunderous serve giving him a 5-2 lead before a scorching forehand into the corner took him to match point.
Zverev then wrapped up victory with his 13th ace of the game and will now face Dutch veteran Botic van de Zandschulp in the quarter-finals.

item.title: Farmer killed, two injured in Kushtia lightning strike
item.description:
A farmer was killed, and two others were seriously injured in a lightning strike in the Tegharia area under Kanchanpur union of Sadar upazila on Monday afternoon.
The deceased was Toafazzel Hossain, 55, son of Mannan Pradhan of Swastipur village under Alampur union of Sadar upazila.
According to police and local sources, Toafazzel was returning home from his crop field. When he reached the Tegharia field, lightning suddenly struck him around 2pm, leaving him dead on the spot.
Two other people were also seriously injured in the lightning strike. Locals rescued them and admitted them to Kushtia Medical College Hospital.
Alampur Police Camp in-charge ASI Faridul Islam confirmed the matter.

item.title: KCC announces Tk 601.79cr budget for FY 2026-27
item.description:
The Khulna City Corporation (KCC) has proposed a budget of Tk 601.79 crore for the 2026-27 fiscal year, without imposing any new taxes.
KCC Administrator Nazrul Islam Manju on Monday announced the budget at the Shaheed Altaf Auditorium of the Nagar Bhaban.
The proposed budget has a deficit of Tk 29.54 crore as expenditure exceeds projected revenue.
Of the total budget, Tk 211.90 crore has been projected as revenue income against Tk 241.44 crore in revenue expenditure. Government grants under the second component have been estimated at Tk 197.62 crore.
For the 2025-26 fiscal year, KCC had initially set a budget target of Tk 719.50 crore, which was revised to Tk 338.97 crore.
The achievement rate was 71.70 percent for the own-fund component and 38.52 percent for the development fund, with an overall achievement rate of 47.12 percent.
Although the budget has been described as development-oriented, it is largely dependent on government and donor grants as well as the corporation’s own revenue.
Manju attributed the shortfall mainly to changes in the country’s political situation and completion of several major projects.
He said Tk 79.46 crore has been allocated under the special development fund for the current fiscal year, while Tk 150 crore has been earmarked under the Annual Development Programme (ADP).
Of the ADP allocation, Tk 92.87 crore has been earmarked for physical infrastructure, Tk 20.50 crore for public health, Tk 33.13 crore for conservancy, Tk 2 crore for emergency water supply and Tk 1.50 crore for veterinary services.
KCC also plans to plant around 50,000 trees and undertake climate-resilient infrastructure development in low-income settlements, including roads, drains, culverts and latrines.
Manju said Tk 73.36 crore had been allocated from KCC’s own funds for development after meeting its regular establishment costs. Of this, Tk 55.27 crore has been earmarked for infrastructure, BMDF, street lighting, education, sports and culture, social welfare, environment, public health, veterinary and conservancy sectors.

Modern cold storage facility nears completion in Bandarban
item.description:
A modern cold storage facility is nearing completion in Bandarban town, offering a much-needed solution to the annual loss of seasonal fruits and vegetables caused by inadequate storage facilities.
The facility, the first of its kind in the district headquarters, is being constructed by the Bandarban unit of the Chattogram Hill Tracts Development Board (CHTDB) at a cost of Tk 1.85 crore and 56 lakh.
Located in the bus station area of Bandarban town, the cold storage will have a capacity to preserve 50 metric tonnes of fruits and other agricultural produce. Construction of the building has largely been completed, while a generator, electrical connections, cooling equipment and other necessary facilities have been installed.
Officials involved in the project said around 95 percent of the work has already been completed and the facility is expected to become operational soon.
Every year, farmers in Bandarban suffer significant financial losses as large quantities of seasonal fruits and vegetables deteriorate because of the lack of proper storage facilities. The new cold storage is expected to reduce post-harvest losses and allow farmers to store their produce until market conditions become more favourable.
Farmers hope the facility will enable them to avoid distress sales during peak harvesting seasons and secure fair prices for their produce.
Abdus Sattar, a farmer from Bandarban Sadar, said the facility would be a major benefit for local growers.
“Although it has taken a long time, we are happy that a cold storage facility is finally being built. Once it becomes operational, we will be able to preserve our agricultural produce and get better prices,” he said.
Lal Piyan Bom, a mango grower from Bandarban Sadar, said the district produces large quantities of Rangwai mangoes and other fruits.
“Bandarban has considerable potential for fruit cultivation. If we have proper storage facilities, we can preserve the fruits and sell them later at better prices,” he said.
According to project sources, construction began in 2023 and is scheduled for completion in 2026.
Abu Bin Mohammad Yasir Arafat, executive engineer of the Bandarban unit of the Chattogram Hill Tracts Development Board, said the project was progressing as planned.
“About 95 percent of the work has already been completed. Once the cold storage becomes operational, farmers will be able to preserve their fruits and other produce for longer periods and earn more from their sales,” he said.

item.title: Power outage disrupts services at Barisal hospital
item.description:
Frequent power outages are causing patients to suffer at Barisal General Hospital and Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital (SBMCH), disrupting treatment and making it difficult to keep operating theatres and critical care units running.
Patients at the hospital face three to four hours of load shedding a day, according to hospital authorities and patients’ relatives.
The department operates from a five-storey building where about 400 patients are admitted on average each day, accompanied by more than 500 relatives, hospital officials said.
When electricity fails, ceiling fans stop working and the crowded wards quickly become difficult to tolerate, particularly for patients suffering from breathing difficulties and other serious illnesses.
“Because of the large number of patients and relatives, it is already very hot inside,” said Abdul Qayum, who has been staying at the hospital with his daughter for seven days. “When the power goes out repeatedly, it feels like we are being boiled.”
Qayum said he bought a rechargeable fan and brought two hand fans to keep his daughter comfortable.
Hospital Director Brigadier General A.K.M. Mashiul Munir said the Medicine Department is served by a single electricity line, unlike the main hospital building, which has two lines and experiences little load-shedding.
“We have requested the Public Works Department to supply 100 litres of fuel every day,” Munir said. But the department has told hospital authorities that there is no government allocation for generator fuel.
The hospital has repeatedly appealed to the ministry for funding, he said.
“The generator is ready, and if we receive fuel, we will be able to provide backup power and reduce the patients’ suffering,” Munir said.
He could not say when the fuel would be available.
Md Faisal Alam, executive engineer at the Barisal Public Works Department, confirmed that the ministry does not currently allocate funds for fuel to operate the hospital generator.
“We have applied for an allocation. Once the allocation is received, fuel will be supplied through a contractor,” Alam said.
He also could not provide a timeframe for the funding.
Power outages are a particular concern in the hospital’s intensive care unit, where staff must closely monitor critically ill patients whenever electricity fails.
“We become worried about the patients when the power goes out,” a nurse working in the ICU said. “As soon as load-shedding begins, we have to remain extra vigilant.”
Relatives often help by arranging rechargeable fans and other necessities during outages, nurses said.
Patients and their families also face practical difficulties beyond the heat. Rahima Begum, who is staying with her husband on the fifth floor, said power cuts disable the hospital’s lift, forcing her to use the stairs whenever she needs to collect food or medicine.
“We came here to make my husband better, but now we are becoming sick ourselves,” she said.
The Barisal electricity grid is supplying only 50 to 55 megawatts against demand of around 85 to 90 megawatts, according to officials at the grid control room.
Officials said the hospital’s main building is protected from regular load-shedding because it has two electricity connections. The Medicine Department building, with only one connection, is subjected to several hours of outages.
The shortage has exposed vulnerabilities in a hospital that serves hundreds of patients each day. Without fuel for its backup generator, a critical department is left without electricity for hours at a time.
For patients struggling with illness in extreme heat, the simplest of cooling devices have become essential: rechargeable fans and hand fans.

item.title: DMCH doctor assault: Two accused placed on 3-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Monday placed two youths on three-day remand each in a case filed over allegedly assaulting, threatening and demanding extortion from Dhaka Medical College Hospital Professor Dr Md Asadur Rahman.
The accused are Sabbir Hossain, 18, and Fahim Israk Labib, 20.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam passed the order after a hearing in the afternoon. Rokonuzzaman, inspector of the prosecution department, confirmed the matter.
Earlier, Paltan Model Police Station Sub-Inspector Md Atikuzzaman, also the case’s investigating officer, produced the accused before the court and sought 10 days’ remand for each.
According to the remand plea, the accused are active members of an extortion gang operating at various locations in Dhaka and were directly or indirectly involved in the incident. Police said their custodial interrogation was necessary for a proper and impartial investigation.
According to the case statement, Dr Asadur was leaving his chamber at Popular Diagnostic Centre in the capital’s Shantinagar area around 10:00pm on August 17 when he boarded a CNG-run auto-rickshaw.
Shortly after the vehicle started moving, four people intercepted it and demanded that the door be opened. Although the driver was initially told not to open it, he eventually did so.
The assailants then repeatedly beat the doctor, leaving him injured on the head, above both eyes and on various parts of his body.
Hearing his cries, people nearby rushed to the scene and detained one of the suspects, identified as Jibon, while the others fled.
Police from Paltan Model Police Station rescued the doctor and took him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Dr Asadur filed the case with Paltan Police Station on August 18.

item.title: UN: Wildfires, heatwaves endanger air quality, health
item.description:
Wildfires and heatwaves, which generate microscopic airborne pollutants, risk undermining international efforts to improve air quality, protect human health and safeguard nature, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said on Monday.
The United Nations' weather and climate agency underlined the links between air pollution and climate change, which scientists say is leading to more frequent and more intense heatwaves and wildfires.
"Extreme wildfires are increasing, leading to big health consequences because of the high toxicity of smoke," the WMO said in a statement accompanying its latest annual Air Quality and Climate Bulletin.
"Whilst regulations in Europe and North America have reduced industrial and transport PM2.5 emissions, exposure to fire-related PM2.5 has increased."
Particulate matter PM2.5 is composed of microscopic particles and droplets of less than 2.5 micrometres in diameter, which is a health hazard because it can penetrate deep into the lungs and bloodstream.
It is emitted by fossil fuel-driven industrial activities, farming, domestic heating and transport, as well as by wildfires and dust storms.
The report said the world needs to better monitor air pollutants such as aerosol -- including black carbon and microplastics --, fine particles and ground-level ozone.
These pollutants "are not sufficiently monitored even though they are widespread and are potentially harmful to ecosystems", the WMO said.
"(We need) complementary and coordinated policies on air quality and climate because they cannot be dealt with in isolation."
"Air quality and climate change can't be dealt with separately. If one worsens, the other does too," Lorenzo Labrador, from the WMO's Global Atmosphere Watch network of scientists, told AFP.
"In places where there are relatively powerful forest fires, we find a lot of fine particle pollution," he said.
Microparticles generated by burning vegetation are "much more toxic" than those emitted by other sources, even car exhaust, he stressed.
They damage the health of people and wildlife living far from the fire itself because they are carried by the wind, but their poisonous effect is not sufficiently taken into account in air quality assessments, Labrador said.
"Conventional risks models based on total PM2.5 concentrations may underestimate wildfire-attributable mortality by up to 93%," the WMO said.
One study cited in the WMO Bulletin says extreme fire-smoke events have tripled globally since the 1990s, contributing to nearly 100,000 additional deaths per year between 2010 and 2018, although this may be an underestimate.
Another source of air pollution that carries major health risks is ground-level ozone, which accumulates when temperatures rise, atmospheric conditions stagnate, and solar radiation is intense, as seen during recent heatwaves in China, Europe and the southeastern United States.
"This increased exposure to ozone pollution has the potential to lead to tens of thousands of additional premature deaths," particularly due to respiratory diseases, the WMO warned.
Another growing concern is aerosol particles, which can also travel to oceans and continents far from their source.
They can alter the way the atmosphere reflects sunlight, change the chemical properties of land and water, and pollute otherwise clean environments.
"One example is the deposition of black carbon -- or soot -- on snow and ice, which reduces the amount of sunlight reflected by these surfaces and in turn can hasten the melting process," the WMO explained.
Another example is microplastics, formed when plastics break down because of sunlight or other factors, and found virtually everywhere -- in the air, the soil and the oceans.
One simulation in the WMO Bulletin estimates there are "51 million tons for land and 22 million tons for the ocean -- which are in turn a source of microplastics for the atmosphere".
"As plastic production and, critically, mismanaged plastic waste continue to increase," monitoring the airborne paths that carry microplastics from their source and dump them in remote environments will be "crucial", the report said.

item.title: Youth killed in knife attack in Mirpur
item.description:
A youth died while undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) after being stabbed by miscreants in the Shah Ali area of Mirpur in the capital.
The deceased is identified as Mehedi Hasan, 26, son of Mohammad Alam of the Faridganj area of Chandpur district. He had been living in the Shah Ali area of Mirpur.
The incident took place in the early hours of Monday. He was later rescued in critical condition and taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors admitted him to Ward No. 102. Mehedi Hasan succumbed to his injuries at around 6:30am while undergoing treatment.
Inspector Md Habibur Rahman, in-charge of the Dhaka Medical College Hospital Police Outpost, confirmed the death, citing doctors.
He said the body has been kept in the hospital morgue for an autopsy. The matter has also been reported to the police of the concerned police station.
He further said: “We have learned that Mehedi Hasan was critically injured after being stabbed by miscreants in the Shah Ali area of Mirpur. He was subsequently rescued and taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he died in Ward No. 102 while undergoing treatment this morning.”

item.title: Man shot dead at Dhaka’s Jatrabari
item.description:
A 32-year-old man was shot dead and another injured in an attack by some criminals in the Dhalpur area of Jatrabari in the capital early Monday.
The deceased was identified as Imran, son of Khokon Ali, a resident of Sardar Goli in Dhalpur, while the injured person was identified as Mohammad Zakaria, 33, of North Dhalpur.
Hospital sources said Imran sustained a gunshot wound to his head, while Zakaria was shot in his leg.
Both were taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH), where doctors declared Imran dead at around 12:07am.
Zakaria is receiving treatment at the hospital.
Quoting Zakaria, police said six to seven helmet-wearing attackers opened fire at a youth in North Dhalpur while shouting, “Imran, don’t run.”
Zakaria said he was also hit by a bullet in the leg during the attack.
According to Zakaria’s wife, Jhinuk Akter, her husband runs a rickshaw garage in Dhalpur Sardar Goli.
Imran and Zakaria were sitting in front of the garage at night when seven to eight helmeted men riding four motorcycles opened fire at them indiscriminately, she said.
Inspector Mohammad Habibur Rahman, in-charge of the DMCH police camp, said Imran’s body has been kept at the hospital morgue for autopsy.

Iran raises price of petrol as US applies economic pressure
item.description:
Iranian authorities on Sunday announced they were raising the price of petrol for heavier consumers, as the United States steps up sanctions seeking to isolate the country's economy.
Iran's quota system prices petrol in three tiers -- 1,500 tomans per litre for a consumer's first 60 litres in a given month, 3,000 tomans per litre for their next 50, and 5,000 tomans per litre after that. The toman is an informal unit equivalent to 10 Iranian rials.
On Sunday, government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani said the price for the third tier would double to 10,000 tomans (about 4.5 US cents).
"The rate will increase to 10,000 toman rials from the morning of September 8," Mohajerani said in remarks carried by state media.
"Different numbers were mentioned in expert meetings, but because the president had promised the people, the rate of 10,000 tomans was set," she added.
She later clarified that the price of the first and second tiers would not be changed.
Iran, a major oil producer with some of the world's cheapest fuel, has for years heavily subsidised petrol, making any changes to pricing politically sensitive.
The development comes as the Iranian currency was trading on the black market Sunday at more than 2.2 million rials to the US dollar, according to websites that track the rate.
Before the start of the Middle East war on February 28, the rial traded at around 1.7 million to the dollar, and in late April it hit what was then a record low of 1.8 million.
Late last month, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, hoping to use financial pressure to hasten the end of the war.
The new measures build on a sanctions regime by the US and allies that has been in place since 2018, when President Donald Trump withdrew from an international deal struck with Tehran on its nuclear programme.
The United States has also put Iran's ports under a naval blockade, attempting to reduce its oil exports to zero.

item.title: Trump suggests renaming New Mexico state 'New America'
item.description:
US President Donald Trump's name-changing spree found an unlikely new target on Sunday when he suggested the state of New Mexico could become "New America."
His proposal, which was immediately dismissed by the state's governor, comes days after he signed an order to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America" in the middle of a trade war with neighboring Canada.
"Many people suggested changing the name of New Mexico... to NEW AMERICA," the Republican president posted on social media. "So much more prestigious and beautiful for the people of that potentially incredible State. Wow, I Love It!!!"
The White House reposted an image showing the Mexico part of the state's name crossed out and replaced with "America."
Some US media reports said the idea originated as an internet hoax.
State governor Michelle Lujan Grisham told Fox News that the name "isn't up for debate -- it's been ours since before the United States existed."
She said the president wanted to "distract Americans" from issues such as soaring gas prices.
Trump last week suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz as "Trump Strait" as the war with Iran continues -- then hours later implied he was not serious about the plan.
He renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America" on his first day back in the White House in 2025 in a move rejected by Mexico.
Canada has also rejected the attempt to rename Lake Ontario.

Study: What children watch matters more than screen time
item.description:
What children do on screens, and whether parents engage with them, may matter more for language development than simply how many hours they spend on digital devices, according to a study that also reveals widespread passive screen use and limited parental involvement among young children.
Titled “Effect of using screen time in developing children’s speech and language: Bangladesh context,” the MPhil study was conducted by Md Zahid Hossain Khan of Dhaka University’s Department of Communication Disorders under the supervision of Professor Dr Hakim Arif.
The study found that 60% of children surveyed spent at least three hours a day on screens, while 80% primarily watched cartoons and other entertainment content.
Yet only 20% of parents consistently stayed with their children during screen use, highlighting a major gap in how digital devices are being incorporated into children’s daily lives.
Researchers found a striking contrast between un-interative viewing and interactive screen use.
Children aged three to five who used educational and interactive apps repeated new words, asked questions and demonstrated improvements in sentence formation.
Those who mainly watched cartoons or YouTube videos, however, showed less inclination to communicate, with some crying or becoming stubborn when the screen was taken away.
The findings challenge the tendency to judge children’s digital exposure solely by the number of hours spent in front of screens, suggesting that the quality of content, active participation and parental interaction can be critical factors.
The research covered 50 children aged three to eight and an equal number of parents and caregivers in Dhaka, Chittagong and Tangail.
In addition to a survey, researchers directly observed each child for 30 minutes while they used a screen.
The findings show that 40% of the children spent three to four hours a day on screens, while another 20% spent more than four hours.
Mobile phones dominated their digital exposure, used by 90% of the children.
Television was used by 70% and tablets by 50%.
Around 80% primarily watched cartoons and entertainment programs, while 60% of children spend time sitting inactive in front of screens rather than actively interacting with the content.
Among children aged six to eight, researchers observed greater discussion about what they watched, although their sentence structures were comparatively weak.
The study also identified parental involvement as a key concern.
Only one in five parents always accompanied their children during screen use, while just 30% actively regulated screen time.
Half of the parents surveyed believed excessive screen use negatively affected language development, while 60% reported a decline in their children’s vocabulary.
At the same time, 60% believed screens could help children learn language when used appropriately.
“Two-way conversation is a key condition for language learning, while screens can turn communication into a one-way process,” Zahid said.
“If parents sit beside their children and talk about the content, screen time is no longer merely screen time; it becomes part of the learning process.”
The findings therefore suggest that parental engagement can change the nature of screen exposure: rather than children simply consuming content, conversation, questions and responses can turn it into an interactive learning experience.
Professor Saiful Alam Chowdhury of the University of Chittagong said the study recommended age-appropriate limits on screen use, development and promotion of quality educational content in Bangla, training for parents and teachers, and government-led awareness programs.
Professor Dr Hakim Arif said children’s growing exposure to screens had emerged as a major challenge to healthy development.
“There has been little long-term scientific research on the issue in our society. I believe this research will play an important role in addressing that gap,” he said.
The findings point to a broader challenge for parents as digital devices become increasingly embedded in childhood: managing screen use may no longer be simply about limiting hours, but also about determining what children watch, how they interact with it and whether adults remain engaged in the process.

item.title: South Korea provides 15,000 tons of rice for Rohingyas
item.description:
South Korea has provided Bangladesh with 15,000 metric tonnes of rice and 150 metric tonnes of fortified rice kernels to support Rohingya refugees.
The rice was handed over at a ceremony on Thursday at the World Food Programme’s (WFP) Sagarika warehouse in Chittogong.
The assistance, provided through the Republic of Korea’s Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA), will support the WFP’s food assistance programme for Rohingya refugees in Cox’s Bazar.
It follows Korea’s previous contributions of 15,000 metric tonnes in 2024 and 20,265 metric tonnes in 2025 to the Rohingya response.
This year’s contribution also includes 150 metric tonnes of fortified rice kernels containing essential vitamins and minerals. The kernels will be blended with the donated rice to enhance its nutritional value, particularly for children and other vulnerable groups. The blended rice will then be transported to Cox’s Bazar and distributed through WFP’s general food assistance programme.
“On behalf of Bangladesh, we sincerely appreciate the Korean government and people for this valuable contribution,” said ABM Shafiqul Haidar, additional secretary at the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief. “It reflects our enduring friendship and shared commitment to addressing humanitarian challenges and supporting those in need.”
“We are pleased to continue Korea’s support for Rohingya refugees through this contribution of rice and fortified rice kernels. By adding essential micronutrients to food assistance, we hope to support not only food security but also better nutrition outcomes for vulnerable families,” said Kim Ji-joon, ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Bangladesh.
“Korea remains committed to working with the Government of Bangladesh and WFP to support the Rohingya community during this difficult time,” he added.
Coco Ushiyama, WFP representative and country director in Bangladesh, said the contribution came at a critical time as humanitarian needs continue to outpace available resources.
She said the assistance would help ensure that Rohingya families continue receiving essential food support, while the fortified rice kernels would improve the nutritional quality of assistance for vulnerable refugees.
“We are grateful to the Republic of Korea for its continued support and solidarity with Rohingya families who remain heavily dependent on humanitarian assistance.” She added.
Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya refugees remain dependent on humanitarian assistance, with limited livelihood opportunities and no immediate prospect of a safe, voluntary and dignified return to Myanmar. Sustained donor support remains essential to maintaining food security and nutrition for one of the world’s largest and most protracted refugee populations.
The Republic of Korea and WFP have worked together for more than six decades, beginning when Korea itself benefited from WFP assistance. Today, Korea is a major provider of in-kind food assistance to WFP operations worldwide. In 2025, MAFRA provided 150,000 metric tonnes of rice to support WFP operations in 17 countries, including Bangladesh.
As the Rohingya crisis enters its 10th year, continued international support remains crucial to sustaining food and nutrition assistance for refugees and supporting the Government of Bangladesh and host communities, which have shouldered responsibility for hosting the Rohingya population for nearly a decade.

item.title: Three of a family drown in Lakshmipur
item.description:
Three members of the same family, including two children, drowned in a pond in Lakshmipur’s Sadar upazila on Sunday afternoon.
The deceased were Abu Siddique Patwari, 65, and his grandchildren Piyas, 8, and Prema, 7. The two children were Abu Siddique’s grandson and granddaughter, born to his son and daughter, respectively.
According to locals, Abu Siddique went to the pond at Patwari Bari in Shakchar union to bathe with his grandchildren around noon. At one point, all three drowned and went missing.
Family members later began searching for them and, with the help of locals, recovered their bodies from the pond.
The deaths have cast a pall of grief over the area, with relatives mourning the tragedy.
Wahid Parvez, officer-in-charge of Lakshmipur Sadar Police Station, confirmed the incident, saying police were sent to the scene after receiving the report. Further details would be available later.

Body of Bangladeshi killed in Lebanon drone strike reaches Satkhira
item.description:
The body of a Bangladeshi worker from Kalaroa upazila of Satkhira, who was killed in a reported Israeli drone strike in Lebanon, reached his village home on Sunday morning, plunging his family and neighbours into grief.
The deceased was identified as Shuvo Das of Shripatipur village in the upazila.
His body reached home around 10am, about three months and 25 days after his death in a drone strike in a conflict zone in southern Lebanon on May 11.
Shuvo was the second of four siblings, including three brothers and a sister.
His family said he went to Lebanon about two and a half years ago after selling two decimals of their homestead land to meet the cost of migration. He has now returned home in a coffin, leaving his family devastated.
He will be cremated at a local cremation ground after noon.
Shafiqul Islam, 43, of Purbapara village in Sadar upazila, and Nahidul Islam, 22, of Kadakathi village in Ashashuni upazila, of Satkhira were also killed in the Israeli drone strike.
Their bodies reached their respective villages on June 7.
Moin Uddin, a counsellor at the Khulna divisional office of the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, said the government provided the family with a cheque for Tk85,000 on Saturday night.
He said the family will receive another Tk3 lakh this month and additional Tk10 lakh from life insurance after a few months.

item.title: 8 arrested over Tk38 lakh robbery in Dhanmondi
item.description:
Police have arrested eight alleged members of a robbery gang in connection with the armed robbery of Tk38 lakh in Dhanmondi, Dhaka.
Deputy Commissioner of the DMP Media and Public Relations Division Md Akter Hossain confirmed the arrests on Sunday.
The arrested individuals are Tanvir Abedin alias Jui, 41; Md Mojibur Rahman, 60; Md Zakir Hossain alias Captain Zakir, 60; Md Solaiman Mridha, 55; Mohammad Kabir Hossain, 50; Abul Kalam Azad, 50; Md Zakaria Hossain alias Lenin, 40; and Sajal Chowdhury, 31.
According to Dhanmondi police, a group of 8-10 people robbed Md Khorshed Alam, 50, of Tk38 lakh at gunpoint around 2:10pm on August 30, 2026.
The robbery took place on the paved road in front of Dingi Restaurant on Road 12/A under Dhanmondi Model police station.
As the robbers fled with the money, Tanvir Abedin and Mojibur Rahman were arrested with the help of police and local residents. A locally made revolver and four rounds of ammunition were recovered from their possession.
Based on information provided by Mojibur Rahman, police later conducted an operation in the Dakshinkhan police station area and arrested Zakir Hossain alias Captain Zakir.
Police subsequently used information provided by the arrested suspects and information technology to conduct raids in different parts of the country, arresting five more alleged members of the gang — Solaiman Mridha, Mohammad Kabir Hossain, Abul Kalam Azad, Zakaria Hossain alias Lenin and Sajal Chowdhury.
During the operations, police recovered Tk345,350 from Zakaria Hossain alias Lenin and Tk230,000 from Sajal Chowdhury.
A total of Tk575,350 of the looted money was recovered and seized.
Police said operations are underway to arrest the remaining absconding and unidentified members of the gang and recover the rest of the stolen money.
A robbery case and a separate case under the Arms Act have been filed with Dhanmondi Model police station in connection with the incident.

item.title: Salahuddin: Global support crucial for sustainable Rohingya solution
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday said a quick and sustainable political solution to the Rohingya crisis requires strong cooperation from the international community and international organizations.
He urged the UN and the international community to keep the Rohingya crisis on the global agenda and ensure that it is not overshadowed by other global conflicts or crises.
“Through joint efforts and effective diplomacy by the international community, we must ensure the rapid and dignified repatriation of Rohingya refugees to their homeland in Myanmar,” the minister said while addressing a round-table discussion titled “The Rohingya Crisis: Emerging Challenges & Reframing Response Strategies.”
The Institute for Global Cooperation Foundation (IGCF) organized the program at the auditorium of the Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS).
Salahuddin said a permanent and sustainable solution to the crisis is possible with the direct support of leading countries in global politics and the UN.
He urged international human rights organizations, the UN high commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and all other relevant stakeholders to play a more effective role in resolving the Rohingya crisis.
“Our main goal is one – to ensure that the nearly 1.5 million Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMNs) currently taking shelter here can be sent back to their own country with full dignity and security,” the minister said.
“For this, continued support from the international community and the political role of leading countries are extremely important,” he said.
Highlighting the long-term impact of the crisis, Salahuddin said Bangladesh has been providing shelter, food, land, healthcare and basic security for livelihood to more than 1.5 million displaced Rohingyas on humanitarian grounds for over nine years.
“But over time, criminal activities, arms and drug smuggling, human trafficking, gender-based violence and activities of armed groups have increased in the camps, creating serious challenges to Bangladesh’s internal security,” he said.
Noting that the lives and environment of local communities living near the camps have also come under serious threat, the minister said necessary security measures such as fencing around the camps and a well-regulated movement system have become essential to control crime and ensure the overall security of both the Rohingya population and local citizens.
“The present government, under the capable and far-sighted leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, is determined to implement a 100% successful repatriation,” he said.
A “National Strategy Formulation Committee on Rohingya Affairs” has already been formed under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Salahuddin said, adding that another high-level national committee, headed by himself, is active in maintaining law and order, border management and overall coordination.
“The government is working with a comprehensive whole-of-government approach involving the civil administration, security and defence agencies,” he said.
The minister warned that humanitarian assistance provided indefinitely without a specific and credible repatriation plan could reduce the pressure for a political solution in the long run.
“Therefore, going beyond emergency relief assistance, we need to move quickly towards a "transitional strategy", whose main objective will be to create a safe and suitable environment in Myanmar’s Rakhine State for the Rohingyas to return,” he said.
Salahuddin expressed hope that through a combination of sustainable international engagement, national unity and a strong security framework, Bangladesh will soon be able to ensure the dignified and permanent repatriation of Rohingyas to their homeland.
Prime Minister’s Adviser on Public Administration Md Ismail Zabihullah delivered a speech as the guest of honour, while State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam attended the program as a special guest.

item.title: Buet student Sunny murder: Case report postponed for 43rd time
item.description:
A Dhaka court has postponed the submission of the investigation report in the murder case of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Buet) student Tarikuzzaman Sunny to October 6, marking the 43rd delay in submitting the report.
The report was scheduled to be submitted on Sunday. However, the investigation officer, SI Mashiur Rahman of Qutubpur Naval Police Outpost, failed to submit it. Following a petition seeking more time, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate of Dhaka Mahbubur Rahman set October 6 as the new date.
SI of the Prosecution Department Mazharul Islam confirmed the matter.
On the afternoon of July 14, 2022, Tarikuzzaman Sunny, a fifth-year student of the Department of Architecture at Buet, went missing while visiting Moinat Ghat in Dohar with 15 friends.
Sunny, son of Harun Or Rashid, was a resident of Hazaribagh in Dhaka.
After he went missing, a diving team from the Fire Service and Civil Defence headquarters conducted a search. Despite extensive efforts that night, he could not be found. His body was recovered from Moinat Ghat at around 11:26am on July 15.
Sunny’s elder brother Hasanuzzaman filed a murder case that afternoon, accusing the 15 friends who had been with him at the ghat.
The accused were arrested after the case was filed and are currently out on bail.
They are Shariful Hossain, Shakil Ahmed, Sejan Ahmed, Rubel, Sajeeb, Nurzaman, Nasir, Maruf, Ashraful Alam, Jahangir Hossain Liton, Noman, Zahid, ATM Shahriar Momin, Maruful Haque Maruf and Roknuzzaman alias Jitu.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir lauds Japan’s efforts for durable Rohingya solution
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Sunday appreciated Japan's efforts toward achieving a durable solution through the safe, voluntary, sustainable, and dignified repatriation of the Rohingyas to Rakhine State in Myanmar.
He also appreciated the Nippon Foundation and Japan's humanitarian assistance for the forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals.
The state minister said Bangladesh remains firmly committed to working with the international community to resolve this prolonged humanitarian and regional challenge.
He made the remarks when Honorary Chair of the Nippon Foundation of Japan Yohei Sasakawa paid a courtesy call on him at his office.
During the meeting, Yohei Sasakawa mentioned that the relationship between the Nippon Foundation and the People's Republic of Bangladesh is built upon a history of profound friendship and mutual trust that spans over half a century, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
“Our cooperative efforts began in 1971 with emergency relief for displaced persons during your nation's independence,” he said.
"Since then, we have consistently stood by the people of Bangladesh, supporting various developmental, healthcare, and educational initiatives. In recent years, our attention has been heavily dedicated to the Rohingya humanitarian crisis," Sasakawa noted.
He informed the State Minister that for over 40 years, he and his organisation have been closely involved in efforts to eliminate leprosy, working in close cooperation with the World Health Organization (WHO), governments, international organizations and NGOs, and organizations of persons affected by leprosy.
They wish to assist leprosy patients in Bangladesh.

item.title: Rangpur shrine caretaker murder: Death sentences upheld for 2, 5 acquitted
item.description:
The High Court on Sunday acquitted five people and upheld the death sentences of two others in the murder case of Rangpur shrine caretaker Rahmat Ali, 60.
The death sentences of JMB commander Masud Rana and Liton Mia were upheld.
The five acquitted by the High Court are JMB members Ishaq Ali, 34; Sakhawat Hossain alias Rahul, 30; Sarwar Hossain Sabu alias Mizan, 30; northern region commander Bijoy alias Ali alias Dorji, 30; and Chandu Mia, 20.
The High Court bench of Justice Zafar Ahmed and Justice Sathika Hossain delivered the verdict on Sunday.
Advocate SM Shahjahan and Barrister Anwar Hossain represented the accused before the court.
In 2018, a Rangpur court sentenced seven accused to death and acquitted six others in the case. Rangpur Special Judge Naresh Chandra Sarkar delivered the verdict.
The seven sentenced to death were JMB's Rangpur region commander Masud Rana alias Mamun alias Montri, 33; Ishaq Ali, 34; Liton Mia alias Rafiq, 32; Sakhawat Hossain alias Rahul, 30; Sarwar Hossain Sabu alias Mizan, 30; northern region commander Bijoy alias Ali alias Dorji, 30; and Chandu Mia, 20.
The six acquitted by the trial court were JMB members Abu Sayeed, 30; Toufiqul Islam Sabuj, 35; Sadat alias Ratan Mia, 23; Jahangir Hossain alias Rajib Gandhi, 26; Babul Akhtar alias Babul Master, 35; and Rajibul Islam Molla alias Badal alias Badhan, 25.
Two of the 13 accused, Chandu Mia and Rajibul Islam Molla alias Badal alias Badhan, were absconding.
Rahmat Ali, the caretaker of a shrine, was hacked indiscriminately and had his throat slit at Chaitar Mor in Madhupur union of Kaunia upazila, Rangpur, while returning home on the night of November 10, 2015.
The following day, his son Shafiqul Islam filed a murder case with Kaunia Police Station.

item.title: Community Bank’s Clean Dhaka Project promotes cleanliness and tree plantation
item.description:
With the theme “Amar Shahor, Amar Desh— Poricchonnotay Bodle Zabe Bangladesh,” Community Bank Bangladesh PLC. organized cleanliness and tree plantation programs under its ‘Community Bank Clean Dhaka Project’ with the aim of building a clean, green and livable Bangladesh.
The programs were held on Saturday at Viqarunnisa Noon School & College and Rajarbagh Police Lines School & College in the capital.
Around 500 students and teachers of the two educational institutions, along with officials and employees of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC participated in the programs.
With the active participation of the students, cleanliness drives were conducted on the premises and surrounding areas of the two institutions, while saplings of different species were also planted.
Dhaka South City Corporation Administrator Md Abdus Salam; Inspector General of Police, Bangladesh and chairman of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC Md Ali Hossain Fakir; Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed; and managing director of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC Mohammed Emtiaz Uddin, along with senior officials of Bangladesh Police, directors of Community Bank, principals of the two educational institutions and other distinguished guests, attended the programs.
Speaking at the event, Inspector General of Police, Bangladesh and chairman of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC Md Ali Hossain Fakir stressed the active role of the younger generation in cleanliness, greenery, tree plantation, personal awareness, drug prevention and maintaining law and order.
“Cleanliness and greenery are among the key prerequisites for a beautiful and livable city. It is not enough to keep roads, streets and our surroundings clean; we must plant more trees to make our cities greener and take care of every tree we plant. A tree not only helps maintain environmental balance, but also ensures clean air, shade and a better environment for future generations,” he said.
Dhaka South City Corporation administrator Md Abdus Salam said: “Nature is behaving adversely because the balance of nature has been disrupted. There is no alternative to planting trees if we want to protect our country and nature.”
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed said: “A collective effort is needed to build a clean Dhaka. It is extremely important to engage the younger generation in such social activities.”
Mohammed Emtiaz Uddin, managing director of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC, emphasized the need to initiate change from within oneself.
As part of efforts to sustain cleanliness practices, 20 dustbins, 20 shovels and 20 brooms were provided to each of the two educational institutions. In addition, 12 fruit-bearing, timber, medicinal and flowering trees were planted at each institution.
Among others, AKM Awlad Hossain, additional IG (Admin), Bangladesh Police and director, Community Bank Bangladesh PLC; Sarder Nurul Amin, additional IG (Special Branch), Bangladesh Police and director; Kazi Md Fazlul Karim, additional IG and rector, Police Staff College and director; Md Kamrul Ahsan, DIG (Confidential), Bangladesh Police and director; Ahmad Muyeed, additional DIG, Bangladesh Police Kallyan Trust and director; Kamrul Hasan Talukdar, inspector, Bangladesh Police and director; Syed Rafiqul Haque, independent director; Syed Rafiqul Haq, independent director, and Mohammed Tofazzul Hussain, independent director, Community Bank Bangladesh PLC, were present at the program.
Also, present were Mazeda Begum, acting principal, Viqarunnisa Noon School & College, and Ahmed Seheli Naznin, acting principal, Rajarbagh Police Lines School & College.

item.title: Large-scale manufacturing sees 14.5% growth in June
item.description:
Large-scale manufacturing rebounded sharply with a 14.5% expansion in June, the final month of FY26.
It provides a stronger-than-expected end to a volatile FY26 marked by repeated contractions amid economic uncertainty, according to official statistics.
The June spike in the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) of large-scale manufacturing suggests that the country's industrial sector may be regaining momentum after a prolonged period of weakness.
Large-scale manufacturing accounts for more than 11% of gross domestic product or GDP of the country, making its performance an important indicator of broader economic activity.
The rebound, however, was not broad-based.
Much of the June growth came from the clothing industry, which carries a dominant 61% weight in the manufacturing index.
The textile sector, the second-largest component with an 11% weight, remained almost stagnant during the month.
The concentration of growth in garments raises questions about the strength of the wider industrial recovery.
While the performance of the clothing industry provided a substantial liftoff to the overall index, several other manufacturing segments continued to struggle, suggesting that the recovery remains uneven.
Some industries are benefiting from stronger demand and export opportunities, while others continue to face subdued consumption, high production costs, financing constraints or weak investment.
The sharp rise in June, therefore, needs to be viewed in the context of the sector's performance over the entire fiscal year rather than as evidence of a fully established recovery.
The sector recorded negative growth in October, November, December, February, March and May. January and another month recorded virtually flat performance.
As a result, the strong June expansion came after months in which manufacturers faced weak demand, uncertainty over investment and disruptions to business activity.
Against this backdrop, the June increase of 14.5% is significant.
It marks a sharp turnaround from the contractionary trend seen during much of the fiscal year and could indicate that manufacturers are responding to improving business conditions and stronger external demand, particularly for export-oriented products.
Among the 23 major manufacturing groups, a number of industries recorded noteworthy performances during June.
They include food products, leather, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, rubber and plastics, basic metals, electrical equipment, machinery, motor vehicles, other transport equipment, furniture and other manufacturing.
The performance of these industries points to some degree of breadth in the June recovery, although the dominant contribution from garments means the overall picture remains heavily influenced by one sector.
Several industries, meanwhile, continued to perform poorly. Among those included beverages, tobacco, wood products, paper and paper products, fabricated metal products, computers and electronics, and printing.

item.title: BKMEA: Withdraw ban on knit fabric import
item.description:
The Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) has urged the government to immediately withdraw a provision in the new import policy for 2026-29 that prohibits the import of knit fabrics.
In a letter to the commerce minister on September 2, BKMEA President Mohammad Hatem expressed concern over sub-clause 12 of provision 25 of the policy, which states that "knit fabrics shall not be importable."
According to the letter, authorities had acknowledged during previous consultations with industry stakeholders that the restrictive provision was included inadvertently and assured the industry that it would be removed.
However, the restriction remained in the official gazette published by the commerce ministry on August 24, 2026.
The BKMEA chief highlighted that the ongoing gas crisis has severely disrupted domestic textile mills and fabric production.
As such, local manufacturers are unable to meet the volume, specialized technical standards and design variations required by international buyers, making raw materials import unavoidable.
The association also noted that several garment exporters had opened letters of credit for raw knit fabrics before the gazette was published.
Many of those shipments have already arrived at Chittagong Port or are in transit, according to the letter.
BKMEA warned that enforcing the ban would prevent customs clearance, causing shipment delays, financial losses and potential cancellation of export orders.
It urged the government to immediately suspend or repeal the provision to ensure uninterrupted production and fulfillment of buyers' commitments.

item.title: Remittance inflow up 18.6% to $6.05bn in FY27

On September 2 alone, expatriate Bangladeshis sent home $108 million through formal banking channels.
The sustained growth in remittance inflows is expected to help strengthen the country's foreign exchange reserves and support external-sector stability.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 13th among cities with worst air quality
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 13th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Sunday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 107 at 9:30am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups”, posing health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
Malaysia's Kuching topped the global pollution ranking with an AQI of 229, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 182 and Uganda's Kampala with 154.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is categorized as "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: IGP urges students to become honest, humane
item.description:
Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir on Saturday urged students to build themselves as individuals with honesty, morality and human values.
“Merit helps a person move forward, but honesty, humanity and moral values make a person truly great,” he said while speaking as the chief guest at a scholarship distribution ceremony for children of police personnel who secured GPA-5 in the SSC, HSC and equivalent examinations in 2024 and 2025.
Police Headquarters organised the program at the Bangladesh Police Auditorium at Rajarbagh Police Lines in the capital. The scholarships were funded by the Bangladesh Police Welfare Trust.
The IGP said the recognition was not merely an award but a recognition of the students’ merit and hard work, the authorities’ confidence in their future and trust in their potential.
Fakir also warned them against drugs, saying they must remain alert against temporary curiosity or provocation that could lead them into addiction.
“Drugs are a deadly trap,” he said, adding that excessive addiction to mobile phones, social media and internet games could be as harmful as addiction to other intoxicating substances.
“Use technology, but remain alert so that technology cannot use you,” he said urging them to obey the law and encourage others to do the same.
Scholarship recipients Kazi Md Tanan Hossain, Syeda Sabiha Musharrat Mumu, Md Adnan Zawad and Mustaina Manzur shared their feelings at the event. Among the guardians, Additional DIG Shampa Yasmin and Police Inspector Sheikh Farukuzzaman also spoke.
A total of 801 students who secured GPA-5 in the 2024 SSC examinations and 272 in the HSC examinations received scholarships. In 2025, 845 SSC and 195 HSC GPA-5 achievers received the scholarships. 2,113 students received Bangladesh Police scholarships in the two years.
Of them, 360 Dhaka-based students were formally awarded scholarships at Saturday’s ceremony. The remaining scholarships will be distributed through the respective district police superintendent’s offices.

item.title: DMP files 3,206 cases for traffic violations
item.description:
The traffic division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) on Saturday filed 3,206 cases against vehicles for violating traffic rules during the last two days in the capital.
The cases were filed as part of the DMP's regular enforcement campaign carried out on Thursday and Friday aimed at ensuring traffic discipline, reducing congestion and improving road safety across the city, according to a media and public relations division issued on Saturday.
The DMP said such drives against traffic law violators will continue, urging motorists and pedestrians alike to comply with traffic regulations to help maintain order on the roads.
It said that the DMP traffic police dumped 878 motor vehicles and towed 501 vehicles during the campaign. During the drives, the Traffic-Ramna Division filed 215 cases, including 19 against buses, 10 covered vans, 16 CNG-run auto-rickshaw and 71 motorcycles, according to a media spokesperson of the DMP.
The spokesperson said 228 cases were filed by the Traffic-Lalbagh Division including against 14 buses, 14 trucks, two covered vans, 13 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 118 motorcycles, while Traffic-Motijheel Division filed 512 cases, against 29 buses, two trucks and 269 motorcycles.
Meanwhile, the Traffic-Wari Division filed 445 cases, including 50 against buses, 41 trucks, 31 covered vans, 50 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 159 motorcycles.
The Traffic-Tejgaon Division filed 244 cases, including 13 against buses, one truck, eight covered vans, 24 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 106 motorcycles.
The Traffic-Mirpur Division filed 669 cases, including 25 against buses, 22 trucks, 47 covered vans, 72 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 258 motorcycles, Uttara division registered 612 cases including against 52 buses, 19 trucks, 23 covered vans, 54 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 261 motorcycles.
The Traffic-Gulshan Division filed 273 cases, including 39 against buses, six trucks, eight covered vans, 29 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 73 motorcycles.
The drives were conducted as part of the DMP's ongoing efforts to enforce traffic laws and ensure discipline on the city's roads, the DMP release said.

item.title: PM: Some political parties trying to create anarchy by exploiting crises
item.description:
Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman on Saturday accused some political parties and individuals of trying to create anarchy by exploiting the country’s ongoing power and gas crises inherited by his administration, saying everyone should act within their limits.
“We are trying to resolve all the problems we have inherited, whether from the authoritarian regime or the interim government,” he said while speaking at a discussion meeting marking the BNP’s 48th founding anniversary.
Tarique Rahman acknowledged that there are problems in various sectors that are causing suffering to the people.
“But we are noticing that some political parties and individuals are trying in different ways to create confusion by exploiting these problems, and through this confusion they are trying to create anarchy in the country,” he said.
The prime minister said the government will uphold the democratic process and make its utmost effort to maintain democratic principles and ethics.
“But if anyone wants to create anarchy, the law of the country clearly sets out how to control such anarchy. Therefore, as a government—and not just as a government, but as a government elected by the people—I want to make it clear that everyone needs to remain within their respective limits,” he said.
The discussion was held at the auditorium of the Krishibid Institution Bangladesh (KIB) in Farmgate.
At the beginning of the program, participants observed a one-minute silence in memory of BNP founder Ziaur Rahman, former BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia and all those who sacrificed their lives for the country and the party.
The event began with the national anthem, followed by the party anthem and a documentary on the BNP.
President Ziaur Rahman founded the BNP on September 1, 1978. The five-day central program marking the party’s 48th founding anniversary, which began on Tuesday, concluded with Saturday’s discussion.
Tarique Rahman said the BNP inherited a fragile economy, as well as weak health, education and communication systems, after forming the government.
He identified the energy crisis as the country’s biggest immediate problem, acknowledging that many people and industries are suffering from shortages of electricity and fuel.
“I apologize on behalf of the party to all those who are suffering from the shortage of electricity and fuel,” the BNP chief said.
He, however, said the government did not want to use the problems left behind by the previous regime or the interim government merely as excuses.
“We do not want to simply cite these problems as excuses. Rather, we want to present the reality to the people and at the same time take measures so that people do not have to face such problems in the future,” the prime minister said.
He said the BNP has already adopted an action plan to address the energy crisis and prepare the country to withstand possible future global disruptions.
“An action plan requires time to formulate, and implementing it also requires some time,” Tarique Rahman said, adding that the government is taking its measures keeping possible future global crises in mind.
He alleged that a political group operated in disguise during the previous authoritarian regime and that some of its members subsequently admitted their involvement.
The prime minister also accused some political parties of attempting to spread confusion and said such activities could create an opportunity for forces associated with the ousted authoritarian regime to return to the political scene.
“Could it be that those who remained hidden under the authoritarian regime are now, from within that hidden network, trying to incite this anarchy?” he asked.
“If that is the case, then those who are hiding are actually working to bring that authoritarian regime back to the forefront,” Tarique Rahman said.
Calling on all nationalist forces and BNP leaders and activists, he said: “Let us make the people more aware. Let us expose to the people who is taking responsibility for whom and who is trying to protect whom.”
The prime minister alleged that certain political forces had protected or sheltered one another at different points in Bangladesh’s history.
“This politics must be exposed before the people. We have to make it clear to the people. Because we have seen these forces, operating covertly, shielding and sheltering one another at different times over the years and decades—whether in 1971, 1986, 1996, over the past one and a half decades, or even today," he said.
“So today, we have to expose their politics before the people. We have to make it clear to the people," Tarique Rahman said.
He said the BNP had consistently sought to establish a democratic system and uphold the democratic rights of the people since the party’s inception.
“We still firmly believe in this,” the prime minister said, adding that hundreds of thousands of BNP leaders and activists had sacrificed their lives for democracy.
At the same time, he said, the BNP wants to build a humane state and a democracy where no one would face obstacles in exercising their rights.

item.title: Thakurgaon ready to welcome President on first hometown visit
item.description:
Thakurgaon is buzzing with preparations to welcome Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on his first visit to his hometown as President.
Alleys, markets, neighborhoods and roads once familiar to him are now being ready for his arrival with an atmosphere of festivity prevailing. Arches are being erected at various points and decorative lights installed, while administrative officials and employees, political leaders and activists are working round the clock. Municipal workers are also working day and night to make the town clean and orderly.
People are eagerly awaiting the President’s arrival, with growing curiosity and excitement among ordinary residents alongside the extensive administrative preparations.
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is scheduled to arrive in his home district on a two-day official visit Sunday.
The district administration has made extensive preparations for the state visit, public interest and emotion surrounding it appeared even greater.
Security measures have also been strengthened across the district. Members of the Special Security Force (SSF), President Guard Regiment (PGR) and intelligence agencies are working at the field level, while additional security has been put in place at the scheduled venues, along travel routes and in other important areas.
Convener of the President’s Reception Committee Dr Abu Md Khairul Kabir said, “He is not only the President, he is a son of Thakurgaon. After a long time, he is returning to his own people while holding the country’s highest constitutional post.” “His return is a moment of immense pride and emotion for us. We want the people of Thakurgaon to welcome him with love and respect,” he added.
District BNP President Mirza Faisal Amin said the President’s first visit to his home district is a matter of joy, pride and emotion for the people of Thakurgaon. He said the President has a longstanding emotional bond with the people of the district, and his visit has generated widespread enthusiasm and excitement among people from all walks of life.
