item.title: Humaiun: PM to carry 'New Bangladesh' message to UNGA
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will carry the message of a "New Bangladesh" and its progress to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Saturday.
"The prime minister will go to the United Nations with the message of the progress of a New Bangladesh," he told journalists at a hotel in the city this morning.
Kobir also said there was a possibility of a meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and US President Donald Trump during the UNGA engagements.
Turning to Bangladesh-India relations, the state minister said discussions were underway regarding a possible visit by the Prime Minister to India, but no date had yet been finalised.
He said despite outstanding issues between the two neighbours, Dhaka remained committed to resolving differences through dialogue and maintaining constructive relations with New Delhi.
"As a neighbour, we should maintain good relations with India," Kobir said, adding that the door for dialogue remained open despite various problems between the two countries.
On the energy sector, the state minister strongly criticised what he described as 'psychopathic corruption' during the previous government, saying the extent of the irregularities could be understood by examining the sector.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is giving the highest priority to energy security and the government is working sincerely to resolve the existing challenges in the sector.
Regarding the proposed Mecca Pact, Kobir said discussions were continuing and Bangladesh's participation in such an arrangement would not be unusual.
He noted that many countries are currently participating in multiple security arrangements, stressing that Bangladesh's decisions would ultimately be guided by its national interests.
"Based on the national interest, we will go wherever we need to go," he said.
Responding to a question about purchasing Boeing aircraft from the United States, Kobir said no one was putting pressure on Bangladesh to buy the aircraft.
"Boeing aircraft are being purchased from the United States because there is a demand for them, and more will be purchased if necessary," he said.
On Bangladesh's labour market in Malaysia, the state minister said syndicates operating during the Awami League government had negatively affected the recruitment of Bangladeshi workers.
He said the incumbent government had dismantled those syndicates and workers would now be sent to Malaysia in phases.
Asked about reports of Bangladeshi nationals being denied hotel accommodation in Kolkata and consequently spending nights on the streets, Kobir said the foreign ministry would take necessary action if specific cases were brought to its attention.
Lawmaker Emran Ahmed Chowdhury and BNP Central Assistant Organising Secretary Miftah Siddiqui were present.

item.title: Shama: UNGA session to offer major opportunity to brand Bangladesh
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Saturday said the upcoming session of the United Nations General Assembly will provide Bangladesh, under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, with a major opportunity to highlight its national interests, economic potential and development priorities on the global stage.
"It marks a new journey, a new possibility and a new aspiration," she said while addressing a discussion titled "Upcoming UNGA and Branding of Bangladesh" as the chief guest, organised by the Centre for Non-Resident Bangladeshi (Centre for NRB), a non-profit research organization for expatriate Bangladeshis.
Prime Minister Tarique is scheduled to attend the UNGA for the first time since the establishment of the new democratic government.
Following the government's "Bangladesh First" foreign policy, Tarique Rahman is set to present Bangladesh to the international community as a democratic, confident, responsible and promising nation.
The high-level segment of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly is scheduled to begin in New York on September 21.
She said Bangladesh should no longer be portrayed internationally merely through floods, disasters or the repatriation of undocumented migrants.
"Bangladesh has opportunities in tourism, business and investment, and it has the potential to be presented properly on the world map. We are trying to brand Bangladesh in the right way. The government alone cannot do everything; all of us must work together," the state minister said.
She said the significance of the session is heightened by the fact that Bangladesh's Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman will preside over the General Assembly.
"This is definitely a matter of pride for Bangladesh," Shama said, noting that Bangladesh's success in the election came despite Cyprus having worked for more than a decade to secure the position.
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur is now in New York and will take up his responsibilities as President of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly soon, a tenure that will coincide with a crucial period for the world body, including the selection of a new UN secretary-general.
The 81st session of the General Assembly will formally open on September 8, with world leaders expected to gather at UN Headquarters in New York later in the month for the annual high-level general debate.
The state minister credited Bangladesh's diplomatic efforts, including those undertaken by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Bangladesh's mission in New York, as well as the country's stability and democratic government, for playing an important role in the victory.
"Therefore, considering all these aspects, this upcoming session will be extremely important for us," she said.
On the Rohingya crisis, Shama said a dedicated session would be held during the UN General Assembly with the participation of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
She said the crisis has become increasingly complex because of the involvement of the Myanmar authorities, the Arakan Army, regional actors and competing international interests.
"In fact, the problem has deepened. A regional complication has been created. Without international pressure, resolving this problem will become very difficult," she said, urging Bangladeshis abroad and civil-society representatives to help mobilize international support for a sustainable solution.
The state minister said the Rohingya crisis is a big problem for Bangladesh. "But it's not Bangladesh's problem. The problem was not created by Bangladesh."
The state minister also highlighted Bangladesh's reputation at the UN, particularly for its contribution to UN peacekeeping operations.
Turning to the government's economic priorities, Shama said economic diplomacy is a major component of the government's manifesto.
She said the government inherited what she described as a "broken economy" and a "broken banking sector" and that restoring the economy and bringing it onto a sound footing would take time.
She said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has been working from the outset to improve transparency and accountability in the banking sector and create a more investor-friendly environment for both foreign investors and non-resident Bangladeshis (NRBs).
"We want to create an environment where our Bangladeshis will return to invest, and foreigners will also invest here," she said.
The government is also working to simplify investment procedures through digital services and a one-stop mechanism so that investors do not have to visit multiple government offices for different services, she said.
Shama said the government is expanding online facilities for registration, company name registration and other procedures to make doing business easier.
She also highlighted the "One Citizen, One Card" initiative, under which information currently held by different government agencies would be consolidated into a single database and linked to one card for each citizen.
The state minister placed particular emphasis on protecting Bangladeshi migrant workers and curbing illegal migration.
She said the government holds expatriate Bangladeshis and remittance earners in high regard, but illegal migration facilitated by broker networks remains a serious concern.
Bangladeshi migrants have been falling victim to broker cartels while attempting to travel through dangerous routes, including the Mediterranean, under false promises of employment in countries such as Italy and Spain, she said.
"We are addressing this issue, and the current prime minister has taken direct action," Shama said.
She said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has been working closely with the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment to tackle illegal migration.
For the first time, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established a dedicated Migration Wing to address illegal migration and issues faced by Bangladeshi expatriates, she said.
The government is also focusing on sending skilled workers abroad through more effective vocational training and skills development, with the aim of ensuring dignified and legal employment for both men and women, she said.
Shama urged the NRB community to help raise awareness among potential migrants about the risks posed by illegal migration and broker networks.
The state minister said government agencies have begun working at the grassroots level, identifying districts where illegal migration is more prevalent and coordinating with local administrations to tackle the problem.
She said the government is working to simplify visa procedures, including provisions relating to visa-on-arrival, and that the revised policy is expected to be placed before Parliament.
"Everything the prime minister is doing aims to make Bangladesh more investment-friendly," she said.
Shama also stressed the importance of economic diversification, particularly in the energy sector, in view of recent global conflicts and disruptions.
The state minister highlighted the government's focus on the Blue Economy, saying the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has a dedicated Maritime Wing working on the sector.
She also pointed to the introduction of the Creative Economy as a new sector in this year's budget.
The sector, she said, will provide particular opportunities for women entrepreneurs and help bring Bangladesh's art, cottage industries, handicrafts and cultural heritage into the mainstream economy while promoting them internationally.
Centre for NRB Chairperson MS Shekil Chowdhury said the organisation arranged the program as part of its annual World Conference Series to showcase Bangladesh's positive developments to the international community.
He said the series also seeks to deepen Bangladesh's global engagement and encourage expatriate Bangladeshis to invest in the country and remit their earnings through legal channels.

item.title: Shafiqur: On streets until people’s demands are met
item.description:
Leader of the Opposition and Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Dr Shafiqur Rahman on Saturday said they would remain on the streets until the people’s demands are fulfilled, accusing the government of deceiving people and breaking its promises.
“We have taken to the streets to realise the people’s demands. We will return home only after those demands are fulfilled,” he said while addressing a rally at Paduar Bazar Biswaroad in Comilla as part of Dhaka-Chittagong long march led by the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance.
He said people shed blood on the streets in the struggle against authoritarianism but their demands have not yet been fulfilled.
The Jamaat chief said the alliance has taken to the streets to press for implementation of the public mandate in the referendum and the spirit of the July mass uprising. “We have come to the streets to restore gas supplies to your homes and ensure electricity.”
He also questioned whether people are receiving uninterrupted electricity and gas and whether extortion is taking place. He said the country is overwhelmed by drugs and called for effective measures to control the problem.
Jamaat Naib-e-Ameer and Deputy Leader of the Opposition Dr Abdullah Muhammad Taher also addressed the rally, calling for implementation of the alliance’s six-point demand and the referendum mandate.
National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam said uninterrupted supplies of oil, gas and electricity must be ensured. He warned that the government would not be able to remain in office if it fails to meet the people’s basic demands.
Liberal Democratic Party Chairman Colonel (retd) Oli Ahmed said the mandate given by 70 percent of people must be implemented, warning that the government would have to be made to fail if the mandate was not automatically implemented.
Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis Ameer Mamunul Haque said people must remain prepared to face tougher challenges ahead to change their fortunes and take the country in the right direction.
He said the long march marked the beginning of the second phase of the ongoing movement. The Dhaka-Chittagong long march began in the capital on Saturday morning with the alliance’s six-point demands.
After holding roadside rallies at different locations, including Shimrail in Narayanganj, the procession reached Cumilla and held the rally at Paduar Bazar Bishwaroad before heading towards Chattogram.
Leaders of the 11-party alliance and local Jamaat leaders also attended the programme.
Their six-point demands are the implementation of people's verdict in the February 12 referendum, trial of the July 2024 mass killings, resolution of the multi-dimensional energy crisis, measures to control soaring prices of essential commodities, an end to extortion and corruption and improvement of the law and order situation and an end to narrow partisanisation.

item.title: Trump says Iran war is ‘small potatoes’ for US
item.description:
President Donald Trump said Friday that the Iran war was “small potatoes” for the United States, in his administration’s latest bid to play down the conflict ahead of crucial midterm elections.
Trump’s comments came a day after Vice President JD Vance said that “I wouldn’t call it a war” despite an upsurge in clashes between Iran and the United States over the Strait of Hormuz.
“A lot of people don’t call it a war. I call it a military conflict because it’s small potatoes for us,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked about Vance’s remarks.
“It’s not a big thing. We did Venezuela, and we did this,” added Trump, who was surrounded by cattle ranchers invited for the signing of two executive orders on beef processing.
The six-month-old war in which 18 US troops and thousands of Iranians have died has reached a stalemate, with Tehran disrupting shipping traffic in the strategic waterway.
But with fuel prices threatening to cost Trump’s Republicans their control of Congress in November’s midterms, his administration has been trying to minimize the conflict.
Trump said the US was carrying out “intermittent strikes” but that “we’re not fighting right now.”
He reiterated his claims that the United States effectively controlled the Strait of Hormuz and had decimated Iran’s military.
“What we’ve done is amazing. We took over Venezuela and we have essentially taken over Iran,” Trump said.
Pressed on calling the war “small potatoes” when 18 service members died, an increasingly irate Trump compared the Iran war to the years-long US wars in Vietnam and Afghanistan.
“I don’t think it matters what you call it. What matters is the fact we have had tremendous success. We’ve stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon,” he said.

item.title: Russia hits Kyiv airports as Trump peace envoys awaited
item.description:
Russian strikes hit Kyiv’s airports overnight, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Saturday, as US envoys are expected to arrive in the region to discuss a plan to end more than four years of war.
US President Donald Trump said Friday he was sending Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv, in Washington’s latest bid to break a diplomatic stalemate in Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II.
Russia hit a civilian target in the Dnipro region overnight, killing four people, as well as Kyiv’s two airports, Zelensky said, accusing the Kremlin of trying to disrupt the envoys’ visit.
“Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine,” Zelensky said on X, adding there would be “no threats to diplomacy” from the Ukrainian side.
It will be the first time that Trump’s businessman friend Witkoff and son-in-law Kushner have visited war-torn Kyiv since Trump returned to office last year with a pledge to resolve the conflict.
Travelling by plane would be a highly unusual move, with Ukrainian airspace closed since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022. Leaders and officials visiting Kyiv have largely travelled by train.
The envoys are expected in Kyiv on Sunday, a senior Ukrainian official told AFP, while US outlet Axios reported they would meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday.
Trump told reporters that the two negotiators would seek to gauge whether progress was possible towards peace in the conflict.
Peace efforts have stalled due to Washington’s war with Iran, while Moscow and Kyiv have intensified long-range attacks, driving up civilian casualties to levels not seen since the start of fighting.
“I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They’ve done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we’ll do it,” Trump said.
“They’re bringing with them a proposal to end the war,” he said.
The US president would not say whether the plan involved Ukraine ceding territory as he has previously suggested, but added: “We have an idea for peace.”
Witkoff and Kushner, who have been involved in negotiations for ceasefires in Gaza and Iran, have travelled repeatedly to Moscow in previous attempts at diplomacy.
The renewed push for diplomacy comes as Russia and Ukraine pummel each other with long-range missile and drone attacks.
Just hours before Trump’s announcement, a Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine’s SBU security service in central Kyiv, according to Zelensky.
The strike, which Zelensky said was aimed at the office of the agency’s acting chief, was the first on its headquarters since the start of the invasion.
Despite the unprecedented nature of the strike, the Ukrainian president proposed observing a ceasefire with Russia for the duration of the US envoys’ trip.
“There will be no airstrikes on our part, and Russia must reciprocally ensure a ceasefire -- without its own airstrikes -- for the duration needed to conduct these talks,” he said in his evening address.
Russia did not immediately comment on the proposal.
Hours later, Oleksandr Ganzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration, said a Russian strike killed four people and wounded five in the southeastern city of Kamianske.
Zelensky had said on Wednesday that Russian airspace would be “completely unsafe” and filled with Ukrainian drones as long as Moscow continued its war.
On Saturday he said Ukraine would “adjust” its air operations to ensure there was “no threats to diplomacy from our side”.
Witkoff and Kusher’s trip comes more than week after a rare visit to Moscow by CIA director John Ratcliffe, who warned Russia against any attack on Nato member states, according to US media.
Earlier this week, the United States welcomed the Russian finance minister at a G20 gathering in North Carolina.

item.title: Iranian media report explosions in Kharg Island area of Gulf
item.description:
Iranian media on Saturday reported several explosions near the country’s major oil hub of Kharg Island in the Gulf, days after renewed fighting broke out with the United States.
Fars news agency said blasts were heard by its correspondent but that there was no smoke visible, while the SNN news agency claimed “an Iranian tanker was targeted by the US” near the island.
There was no immediate comment from US or Iranian officials.
Fighting between the foes resumed last Sunday with US attacks on Iran as their war passed its six-month mark.
The American strikes prompted retaliatory attacks by Tehran on US targets in the Middle East.
Iran said Thursday that its armed forces had hit US military bases in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates, vowing to avenge civilian deaths at a wedding that it blamed on Washington.
The two sides also remain vying for control of the strategic Strait of Hormuz, with Iran blocking the passage of ships as Washington maintains a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

item.title: One detained after alleged snatching at Mugda hospital
item.description:
A man was detained while allegedly attempting to flee after snatching a mobile phone and a bag at Mugda Medical College Hospital in the capital.
The detained man was identified as Nazmul Alam Biplob.
Md Najmus Sakib, deputy director (public relations) of Bangladesh Ansar, said on Saturday morning that the incident took place around noon on Friday in front of ICU-1 on the hospital’s sixth floor.
Taking advantage of the crowd of critically ill patients and their relatives, Biplob allegedly attempted to flee with the mobile phone and bag.
An Ansar team led by member Md Zakiul Islam, who was on duty at the hospital, caught him in the act, Sakib said.
A search of the suspect led to the recovery of the stolen mobile phone and bag intact, he added.
The matter was subsequently reported to the hospital authorities. Following their instructions, Biplob was handed over to police at the local police station.

item.title: State Minister Abdul Bari sent to Dhaka for advanced treatment
item.description:
State Minister for Public Administration and Food Abdul Bari, who was injured in a road accident in Shibganj, Bogra, while travelling from Dhaka to his constituency in Joypurhat-2 (Kalai-Khetlal-Akkelpur), has been sent to Dhaka for advanced treatment.
The state minister and his wife Najma Ara Begum were injured in the accident on Friday morning. A woman, identified as Firoza Begum, 55, was killed.
Kalai Police Station Officer-in-Charge Saidul Alam said Abdul Bari received primary treatment in Kalai before being admitted to Joypurhat 400-Bed General Hospital. His wife was unharmed and is in good health.
After receiving treatment at the hospital, doctors decided to refer the state minister to Dhaka for advanced medical care. His planned visit to the constituency was cancelled, and he was taken to Dhaka by ambulance at around 12:45pm on Friday.
Dr Rashed Mobarak Jewel, superintendent of Joypurhat 400-Bed General Hospital, said Abdul Bari sustained injuries to both shoulders and his chest in the accident but is now out of danger.

item.title: Asaduzzaman urges Hindu community to unite against injustice, evil forces
item.description:
Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Md Asaduzzaman on Friday urged members of the Hindu community to remain united against any evil or destructive forces and injustice, saying the government is committed to ensuring an environment where every citizen can celebrate religious festivals freely, safely and with dignity.
He made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at a program, marking Janmashtami on the Ramgopal Temple premises in the Shailkupa upazila headquarters.
The minister called upon the Hindu community to stand beside the government against any form of evil or destructive forces. Referring to the teachings of Lord Krishna, he said Krishna appeared nearly 5,000 years ago to defeat evils and oppression and establish peace and justice in society.
“Fighting against injustice and evil forces is the core principle of his teachings. We believe that when we fight to eliminate injustice and evils from society, you will stand beside the government as you have always done,” he said.
Asaduzzaman warned that no attempt to create disorder or obstruct religious programmes will be tolerated. “Religion is for individuals, but security is for everyone. We must move forward with this eternal principle,” he said, adding that law enforcement agencies will take strict legal action against anyone attempting to create disorder, intimidation or obstruction during religious programs.
“There is no distinction between minorities and majorities. Everyone in the country must be able to practise their religions peacefully and without hindrance,” the minister said.
After the discussion, Asaduzzaman joined a colourful Janmashtami procession that began at the Ramgopal Temple and paraded through the main streets of Shailkupa town.
Jhenaidah Deputy Commissioner Md Noman Hossain, Zila Parishad Administrator Md Abdul Majid, leaders of the Puja Udjapan Parishad and Hindu devotees from different walks of life attended the program.

item.title: Nahid: Country is somewhat stable, but needs strong foundation
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) convener and opposition chief whip Nahid Islam has said the situation in the country remains somewhat stable, but a strong foundation must be established to ensure communal harmony, human dignity and stronger democratic institutions.
“We are still continuing that movement,” he said.
Nahid made the remarks at a press briefing after a view-exchange meeting with members of the Sanatan community at Dhakeshwari Temple in the capital on Friday, on the occasion of Janmashtami. NCP Joint Member Secretary and MP Nusrat Tabassum and other central leaders were present.
Nahid said the country had previously witnessed various forms of torture and oppression against minorities and ethnic communities, while the state or government remained silent and failed to take action.
“Sometimes, it indirectly supported them. Due to this, a culture of impunity was created,” he said.
“From that place, after the July uprising, we have repeatedly said that the judiciary must be strengthened. Communal harmony and human dignity must be ensured,” he added.
Nahid said the implementation of the July Charter and the verdict of the referendum would help establish the judiciary on a strong foundation.
“We think that if the July Charter and the referendum verdict are implemented, the country's judiciary will stand on a strong foundation. Through this, there will be a place for people of all communities in the country to get justice,” he said.
“All political forces, including the government and the opposition, must keep this in mind. The culture of impunity must be changed. Political and democratic institutions must be strengthened,” he added.
He said the country had a spiritual bond with people of all religions, including the Hindu community.
“Their festivals are thousands of years old, and the interaction of people of many cultures and religions in this delta has developed through interactive communication. Such a bond must be maintained,” Nahid said.
He called on followers of Sanatan Dharma to pray for the people of Bangladesh and the NCP.

item.title: Health minister vows to make all government hospitals free of brokers
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain on Friday vowed to make all government hospitals in the country free of brokers.
He made the remarks while briefing journalists after inspecting Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital, the 250-bed District Hospital and Shaheed Shamsuddin Ahmad Hospital in Sylhet.
Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir was present at the briefing.
The health minister also directed the authorities concerned to resolve all drainage and cleanliness problems at hospitals in Sylhet within 7 days.
He said a syndicate lures patients to private clinics with false promises.
Sakhawat said all law enforcement agencies, including the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) and Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), are working together to identify and curb such broker syndicates.
“Their activities have already been reduced,” he said.
Regarding the ongoing drive against illegal clinics and fake doctors, he said mobile courts are being conducted regularly in the districts through deputy commissioners and civil surgeons, with illegal establishments being fined and sealed off.
The minister said clinics providing medical services, including surgeries, through unauthorized doctors and technicians holding fake certificates are also being sealed off.
He said he is personally collecting lists of such establishments and supervising the drives against them.
Asked about doctors’ attendance at hospitals, Sakhawat said he has visited more than 25 hospitals over the past month and found doctors fully present.
He added that patients have also reported improvements in doctors’ behavior and the quality of food served at hospitals.
On the measles outbreak, the minister said the number of unvaccinated children in the country has increased as regular measles vaccination campaigns were not held for a long time after December 2020, resulting in the spread of the disease.
He said some children who became eligible for vaccination after the campaign, as well as those who missed vaccination on time due to a lack of awareness, remained unvaccinated, allowing measles to spread among them.
Sakhawat said vaccination activities are continuing with adequate vaccines brought in with support from the World Bank and UNICEF.

item.title: 81 dead as Yemen’s Houthis push towards key strait
item.description:
Clashes between Yemen’s Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces have killed 81, military and medical sources said on Friday, as the Iran-backed rebels push towards territory bordering a chokepoint in the strategic Red Sea.
Fighting erupted on Thursday, after the Houthis launched a ground assault along with rocket and drone attacks near coastal areas, vying for control of the narrow Bab al-Mandab strait at the Red Sea’s southern entrance.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi ships in recent weeks in the Red Sea, which has emerged as an alternative route for oil exports after Iran all but halted shipments from the Gulf by blockading the Strait of Hormuz.
The rebels are now trying to cement their hold over one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, which they have disrupted with attacks on passing vessels since the Gaza war broke out in 2023.
The Houthi offensive aims to cut off the government-held port city of Mokha, under fire for weeks, and advance towards areas bordering the Bab al-Mandab, military sources told AFP.
The rebels have seized elevated sites overlooking government positions near the Red Sea, the coastal town of Khokha and Taiz city further inland, a military source and a Taiz official told AFP, requesting anonymity.
The Houthis could target ships from these elevated positions, they said.
A military official on the coast said 24 of his men had been killed, while another in the Taiz area said 15 had died there. At least 42 Houthi militants were also killed, according to medical sources in areas under their control.
The Houthis want to control the hills overlooking Bab al-Mandab and Mokha before attacking the coast, a Yemeni official in Aden, the government’s base since it was ousted from the rebel-held capital, Sanaa, in 2014.
The government has sent reinforcements to Taiz from Aden on Saudi orders, the official said.
With Iran’s closure of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandab chokepoint has gained increased importance as a transit route for oil from Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest exporter of crude.
The narrow waterway connects the Red Sea -- and, via the Suez Canal, the Mediterranean -- to the Indian Ocean.
Although the Houthis do not control areas bordering Bab al-Mandab, they hold the key port city of Hodeida north of Mokha.
In July, a fragile truce between the Houthis and the government fell apart after the rebels welcomed an Iranian plane to Sanaa, setting off a spate of attacks.
They later announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships and territory as Yemen, following more than a decade of civil conflict, became the latest country drawn into the Middle East war.

Martinelli joins Al-Hilal from Arsenal for reported £60 million
item.description:
Arsenal forward Gabriel Martinelli has joined Saudi side Al-Hilal, the Premier League champions announced Thursday.
No fee was disclosed but British media reports said the deal was worth a guaranteed £60 million ($81 million).
That would make 25-year-old Brazil international Martinelli the most expensive player to leave the London club, following Alex Oxlade Chamberlain's £35 million exit to Liverpool in 2017.
Martinelli has signed a four-year deal with Al-Hilal, who are currently joint-top of the Saudi Pro League with Cristiano Ronaldo's Al-Nassr.
"Gabriel Martinelli has joined Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal on a permanent transfer," said a statement on Arsenal's website.
"Proud to be blue, proud to be Al-Hilal," said Martinelli during an unveiling video on his new club's social media channels.
He will join Ollie Watkins at Al-Hilal after the England striker left Aston Villa in a deal worth an estimated £51 million.
Martinelli's departure comes after Arsenal sold fellow left-sided forward Leandro Trossard to Besiktas.
Christos Tzolis has joined from Club Brugge but there are concerns the exits of Martinelli and Trossard could leave Arsenal short of personnel in that part of the pitch.
Martinelli made 53 appearances in all competitions last season, scoring 11 goals, as the Gunners won the top-flight title for the first time since 2004.
His nearly 300 games for Arsenal, including 62 goals, also saw him involved in their 2020 FA Cup and 2023 Community Shield successes.
But he was left out of Arsenal's first two matchday squads of the season, with manager Mikel Arteta making it clear Martinelli would struggle for game time were he to remain at the Emirates Stadium.
Former Arsenal striker Ian Wright criticised the club's decision to omit Martinelli from the squad for the opening game against Coventry.
"The way Martinelli is being treated at the moment, it really makes me feel uncomfortable," Wright told Sky Sports.
"I know they might want him out, and a lot of people might say, 'yeah, it's time for him to move him on'. But there's ways of doing that and it should suit him as well, how he wants to leave."

item.title: Bangladesh-Russia Parliamentary Friendship Group meets Russian ambassador
item.description:
The Bangladesh-Russia Parliamentary Friendship Group has formally begun work to strengthen bilateral cooperation in parliamentary affairs and capacity building.
Alongside traditional and official diplomacy, the group has been established to strengthen the relationship between lawmakers of the two countries through parliamentary diplomacy and professional exchanges.
On Thursday evening, a delegation from the Bangladesh-Russia Parliamentary Friendship Group held a courtesy meeting with the Russian Ambassador to Dhaka, Alexander Khozin.
The meeting saw fruitful, positive discussions on key aspects of the multifaceted strategic bilateral relationship and multilateral cooperation.
Chairman of the Friendship Group, BNP Vice Chairman and former minister Altaf Hossain Chowdhury recalled with deep respect the historic bond between the two nations. He said Russia has remained one of Bangladesh's most important and tested development partners since the Great Liberation War of 1971. Over time, this historic bilateral relationship has evolved into a strong and trusted partnership. He further noted the need to continue joint and coordinated activities in agriculture, education, technology, nuclear science, food security, the energy sector, and, above all, to strengthen people-to-people connections between the two nations.
He said Bangladesh has historically and deeply believed in the foreign policy of "friendship to all, malice towards none."
He expressed hope that coordination among the new generation and joint initiatives under a new framework would make the Dhaka-Moscow bilateral partnership deeper and more dynamic in the days ahead. Russian Ambassador to Dhaka Alexander Khozin warmly welcomed the Bangladeshi delegation and assured full cooperation between the two countries.
He said Russia would extend all forms of cooperation for any positive initiative aimed at developing parliamentary relations between the two countries, exchanging experience among lawmakers, and building mutual capacity.
He expressed confidence that this joint engagement between members of parliament from both countries would elevate existing trade, economic, and diplomatic ties to new heights. Mia Sattar, President of the Russian Friendship Society with Bangladesh, identified matters of mutual interest as the foundation of the bilateral relationship. He remarked that "mutual benefit" is the real basis of any sustainable, long-term bilateral relationship. He urged that the relationship between the two friendly nations be further strengthened through public diplomacy and social coordination.
He said the Bangladesh-Russia Parliamentary Friendship Group, built on shared interests and mutual benefit, would play a direct role in increasing trust and reliance between the peoples of the two countries. Members of parliament present at the meeting, led by Friendship Group Chairman Altaf Hossain Chowdhury MP, included Khairul Kabir Khokon, Syed Al Noman, Saiful Alam, Atiqur Rahman Mujahid, and Zeba Amin Khan. Also present, as part of institutional and diplomatic protocol coordination, was S.M. Mahbubul Alam, Director General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Eastern Europe and CIS Wing. Alongside Dhaka, a "Group of Deputies" — a parliamentary friendship group led by a Muslim member of parliament — has also been formed in the State Duma, the lower house of Russia's parliament, to improve relations with Bangladesh. Work is continuing there to consolidate good relations between the two countries at the international and public diplomacy levels.
This robust development in parliamentary diplomacy is expected to further strengthen the strategic positions of both countries in various international forums.

Dhaka ranks 6th in global air quality index
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 6th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Friday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 132 at 9:45am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups”, posing health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
Kuching in Malaysia topped the global pollution list with an AQI of 316, followed by Kampala in Uganda with 178 and Jakarta in Indonesia with 158.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is categorized as "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Dengue cases rise alarmingly in Rajshahi region
item.description:
Dengue cases have risen alarmingly across the Rajshahi region, with 1,874 patients receiving treatment at hospitals in the division last month. Of them, 1,339 were treated at hospitals in the eight districts, while 535 received treatment at three medical college hospitals. Two patients died during the period.
Chapainawabganj has recorded the highest number of cases among the eight districts, emerging as a dengue hotspot while Rajshahi Medical College Hospital (RMCH) treated the highest number of patients among the three medical colleges.
According to the divisional health office, Chapainawabganj has recorded 643 cases in August, followed by Sirajganj with 363, Bogra 165, Natore 56, Pabna 42, Naogaon 41, Rajshahi 25 and Joypurhat four.
Among the medical colleges, RMCH treated 228 patients, including the two fatalities. Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital in Bogra treated 88 patients, while Sirajganj Medical College Hospital treated 219.
At RMCH, the number of dengue patients under treatment rose from eight on August 1 to 50 on August 30. During the month, 221 new patients were admitted and 176 discharged. Admissions increased significantly in the second half of August, with 136 patients admitted between August 16 and 30, compared with 85 during the first half.
Hospital authorities said increasing numbers of patients have placed additional pressure on doctors and nurses. In some facilities, patients have been accommodated in corridors after wards became overcrowded.
RMCH spokesperson Dr Sheikh Shamim Ahmed said a 39-year-old man from Chapainawabganj died of dengue on August 30. Another patient died on August 11. By September 2, 19 new patients had been admitted in the previous 24 hours, while 14 were discharged, leaving 60 patients under treatment.
A recent survey in Rajshahi found Aedes larvae in 24 of 75 houses inspected. Of 68 water-holding containers examined, 46 contained larvae. The city’s Breteau Index stood at 61.33, well above the World Health Organization’s high-risk threshold of 20.
Health officials have urged intensified mosquito-control, sanitation, larvicide, fogging and public-awareness campaigns, particularly in Chapainawabganj and Sirajganj.

item.title: Bobby Hajjaj: Midday meal is every child's right, not charity
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj Thursday said providing midday meals to schoolchildren is not an act of charity or favor, but a fundamental right of every child.
"The main objective of the school feeding program is to improve children's health, ensure regular attendance and enhance their learning capacity by providing nutritious food," he said.
He was speaking at an orientation program for head teachers and a discussion on improving the quality of primary education, organized at a local hotel in Khulna under "Feeding Program in Government Primary Schools" project.
Bobby Hajjaj said ensuring nutrition and education for every child is the government's responsibility and warned that no irregularity, negligence or supply of substandard food would be tolerated in implementing the program.
The participation of teachers, parents and local communities in ensuring transparency and accountability in the program would be further strengthened, he added.
Referring to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's vision, the state minister said the school feeding program is playing an effective role in achieving the two key goals of primary education set by the Prime Minister - "No child will remain out of school" and "Every child will be properly educated."
"The government is continuously increasing investment in primary education. The objective is not merely to develop infrastructure, but also to ensure nutrition for every child and build a skilled and educated generation," he added.
On ensuring food quality, Bobby Hajjaj instructed the authorities not to accept or distribute any substandard, rotten or unsuitable food. He said such food should be returned immediately and the concerned Assistant Upazila Education Officer informed.
"If any irregularity is found in the supply system, strict action will be taken after investigation," he warned. He also said the "Mothers' Committee" was being involved more effectively in monitoring the program to strengthen oversight.
Khulna Divisional Commissioner Md Abdullah Harun chaired the meeting. Khulna City Corporation Administrator Nazrul Islam Manju, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education Md Matiar Rahman, Feeding Program Project Director Md Abul Amin and Khulna Deputy Commissioner Hure Jannat attended the program as special guests.

item.title: State Minister Shama urges investment in cosmetics industry
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has called for greater local and foreign investment in Bangladesh’s cosmetics, skincare and personal care industry, saying the sector has the potential to become a major manufacturing and export hub.
She made the remarks while inaugurating Cosmética Dhaka 2026 at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB) in Dhaka on Thursday.
Speaking as the chief guest, Shama Obaed said Bangladesh could leverage the production capacity, compliance infrastructure, skilled workforce and global buyer networks developed through its readymade garment industry to build a competitive cosmetics sector.
“By leveraging the production capacity, compliance infrastructure, skilled workforce and global buyer relationships that we have developed in the readymade garment industry, it is possible to establish contract manufacturing, formulation, specialized packaging, quality laboratories and certification facilities in the cosmetics sector as well,” she said.
She also highlighted the potential of Bangladesh’s agricultural and natural resources.
“If we can build a strong supply chain of certified botanical and herbal ingredients by utilizing Bangladesh’s agriculture and natural resources, this sector will not only meet domestic demand but also open new export opportunities for Bangladesh in the global market,” she said.
The state minister said the government wanted to take the industry beyond “Made in Bangladesh” towards “Formulated, Developed and Branded in Bangladesh”.
She called for investment facilitation, internationally recognized testing and certification, intellectual property protection, sustainable packaging and support for small and medium-sized entrepreneurs.
“If we can establish an integrated industrial base by ensuring environmentally friendly production, safe raw materials and international standards, the cosmetics and personal care sector could emerge as a new and powerful area for foreign currency earnings, employment generation and economic diplomacy in Bangladesh,” she added.
Cosmética Dhaka 2026 features brands, manufacturers, suppliers, retailers and health experts from 16 countries, including South Korea, Thailand, the United States, France, Singapore, China, Japan and India.
The three-day exhibition has more than 100 stalls, along with live demonstrations, beauty consultations, expert discussions and networking opportunities.
BIAA President Baharul Monsur said the cosmetics and personal care industry had been growing every year and called for more investment through the exhibition.
Frank Kenton, senior perfumer at Senses International Ltd, said Bangladesh was one of the promising markets in South Asia, but products must remain affordable for consumers.
SM Faisal Munim, CEO of Squad Mind Global Ltd, said the organizers expected the exhibition to attract more local and foreign investment and establish itself as a business-matching platform.
The exhibition will remain open to visitors from 10am to 7pm every day.

item.title: Thirty injured as picnic bus collides head-on with passenger bus in Natore
item.description:
At least 30 teachers, students and guardians of Shaheen School’s Sirajganj branch were injured when a bus carrying them collided head-on with a passenger bus in Baraigram upazila of Natore on Thursday.
The accident occurred around 10am in the Manikpur area of the Bonpara-Hatikumrul highway as the school group was travelling to Safina Park in Rajshahi for an annual picnic.
The collision left the front sections of both buses badly damaged. Traffic on the highway remained halted for about an hour before the vehicles were removed and movement resumed, reports Bangla Tribune.
According to eyewitness Hossain Ali, the school bus was heading towards Rajshahi when it collided head-on with a Dhaka-bound passenger bus in Manikpur. No one was killed, but at least 30 people travelling on the picnic bus were injured.
The injured include Rezaul Karim, 39; Zainal Abedin, 26; Sinha Islam, 7; Sonali Khatun, 25; Barsha Khatun, 20; Taslim Ahmed, 33; Hazrat Ali, 50; Dighi Khatun, 12; Rabbi Hasan, 24; Ashraful Islam, 42; Beauty Begum, 26; Hawa Begum, 30; Monirul Islam, 33; Habiba Khatun, 12; another Rezaul Karim, 45; Kabya Hossain, 12; and Mostafizur Rahman, 46.
Fire Service personnel from Bonpara, highway police and local residents rescued the injured and took them to Baraigram Upazila Health Complex and Amina Hospital in Bonpara for treatment.
Five teachers of Shaheen School alleged that the passenger bus was travelling recklessly at high speed and suddenly rammed into their bus. Some passengers fell from their seats while others were thrown against the windows, causing panic inside the bus.
The driver of the passenger bus fled the scene following the crash, they said.
The school’s picnic programme has been cancelled following the accident. The injured are being taken back to Sirajganj after receiving treatment.
SI Alamgir Hossain of Bonpara Highway Police Station said the two buses involved in the accident had been seized.

item.title: Ziaur Rahman Medical College interns call off strike
item.description:
Intern doctors at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College (SHZMC) Hospital in Bogra called off their two-day strike on Thursday after authorities assured them of increased security and action against those accused of attacking doctors.
The interns began the strike at midnight on Tuesday after several colleagues were injured when relatives of a patient who died at the hospital allegedly attacked doctors on duty.
They decided to resume work following a nearly three-hour meeting involving political leaders, the district administration and hospital authorities at the hospital auditorium on Thursday.
Intern doctor Ritul Mondal Snigdha confirmed the decision.
SHZMC Hospital Deputy Director Dr Manzur-e-Morshed said the meeting was held in a cordial atmosphere and the interns agreed to return to work after being assured that their demands would be addressed.
Their demands included expelling those involved in the attack who allegedly acted in the name of the Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), increasing police presence, deploying armed Ansar personnel and appointing the required staff for 18 beds.
The interns resumed their normal duties from Thursday night, the deputy director said.
Meanwhile, five JCD leaders were expelled from the organization over their alleged involvement in the incident.
Abdul Malek, of Rajapur village in Bogra Sadar, died while undergoing treatment in the Medicine Ward on the seventh floor of the hospital at around 10pm on Tuesday.
Following his death, his relatives allegedly attacked doctors on duty with locally made weapons. Several doctors were injured, including intern doctor Mohammad Ali Jinnah, who suffered a broken hand, and Azraf Islam, who sustained bleeding injuries.
At a press briefing on Wednesday, the interns said at least 15 of their colleagues had been injured, six of them seriously.
The attackers also allegedly vandalized medical equipment and government property, causing an estimated Tk2.1 lakh in damage. Three mobile phones and a stethoscope were reportedly taken from the ward.
Police rushed to the hospital and brought the situation under control.
Hospital Ward Master Anwar Hossain filed a case with Bogra Sadar police station, naming seven people and eight to 10 unidentified individuals as accused.
Police arrested six people on Wednesday afternoon and, following a court order, sent them to Bogra jail.
While Thursday’s meeting was underway, Bogra city JCD announced the expulsion of five leaders for disciplinary violations.
They are Ward 18 Convener Nafiul Islam, Senior Joint Convener Monir Hossain, Joint Convener Md Pranto Islam, member Rakibul Hasan Rakib and Ward 19 Assistant Organizational Secretary SM Shihab.
District JCD President Habibur Rashid Sandhan said strict organizational and legal action was being taken against those involved in the attack.
The interns’ strike disrupted services at the hospital for two days, although emergency services remained operational. Patients and their relatives travelling from different areas faced difficulties.
At around 10am on Thursday, the interns also closed the outpatient department ticket counter, causing anger among patients and their relatives. The counter reopened after hospital authorities intervened.
During Thursday’s meeting, District Commissioner Toufikur Rahman, Police Superintendent Mirza Sayem Mahmud, District Council Administrator AKM Ahsanul Tayeb Zakir, Bogra City Corporation Administrator MR Islam Swadhin, former SHZMC principal Professor Dr Moudud Hossain Alamgir Pavel, current principal Professor Dr Wadudul Haque Tarafdar, Deputy Director Dr Manzur-e-Morshed, medical leaders, and social and political leaders were present.
Hospital services returned to normal after the interns called off their strike.

item.title: 429 arrested, weapons recovered in DMP raids over 24 hours
item.description:
A total of 429 people were arrested in regular raids conducted by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) across the capital over the past 24 hours.
During the operations, police also recovered several illegal firearms, 822 yaba pills, 19kg 185g of cannabis and 88 bottles of Eskaf syrup. A total of 64 cases were filed during the period.
Deputy Commissioner of the DMP’s Media and Public Relations Division Md Akter Hossain confirmed the information on Thursday.
Four people were arrested in connection with a gunfight in Gandaria, and a foreign-made pistol and yaba were recovered following the incident.
In a separate operation in Banani, five people were arrested with a foreign-made pistol while allegedly preparing to commit a robbery.
In Mirpur, notorious criminal and shooter Zakir was arrested with firearms and ammunition.
Meanwhile, the DMP’s City Intelligence Analysis Division arrested a suspected drug dealer and recovered 7kg of cannabis.
Of the 429 arrested, 22 were detained by the Ramna Division, 22 by the Lalbagh Division, 39 by the Wari Division, 66 by the Motijheel Division, 62 by the Tejgaon Division, 144 by the Mirpur Division, 35 by the Gulshan Division, 39 by the Uttara Division and two by the Detective Branch.
The arrests were made during operations in various police station areas across the capital, where police also recovered other evidence and narcotics.
Legal proceedings against the arrested individuals are underway, the DMP said.

item.title: Madrasa student death: Father protests teacher’s bail, questions suicide theory
item.description:
The father of an eight-year-old madrasa student found hanging in a teachers’ toilet in Jatrabari on Thursday questioned how his son could have died by suicide as a Dhaka court granted bail to one of three teachers accused in the case.
“An eight-year-old child cannot commit suicide. My son could not even tie a mosquito-net rope. How could he hang himself?” Ziaur Rahman said after the court granted bail to Hafez Mohammad Ullah.
He also questioned how the knot around his son’s neck had been tied, saying even a sensible person could not have made such a knot.
Ziaur Rahman was present at the court to oppose Mohammad Ullah’s bail and expressed frustration over the order, as well as the fact that the other two accused teachers have not been arrested.
“They are moving around openly. The law enforcement agencies are not arresting them,” he said.
Dhaka’s 15th Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Mizanur Rahman granted Mohammad Ullah bail after hearing arguments from both sides.
SM Abul Kalam (Azad), lawyer for the complainant, confirmed the matter.
The court granted Mohammad Ullah bail on a Tk1,000 bond until the police report is submitted.
Mohammad Ullah was arrested nearly two months after the case was filed and has remained in jail since then.
During the hearing, his lawyer, Abul Kalam Khan, sought bail, saying his client was not involved in the incident and had been implicated in the case as part of a conspiracy.
He said Mohammad Ullah was the sole earning member of his family and that his detention had left his family struggling.
“Any condition may be imposed for his bail,” the lawyer said.
Opposing the bail, Alhaz Borhan Uddin, chief prosecutor in the BDR mutiny case, said CCTV footage from the madrasa showed the child appearing cheerful and energetic on the afternoon of the incident.
He said it was suspicious that the eight-year-old was later found dead in the teachers’ toilet with a gamcha, a traditional thin cotton towel, around his neck.
“The accused killed the child. We oppose his bail,” he said.
Child found dead in teachers’ toilet
On December 20 last year, Mudachchir’s body was recovered from the teachers’ toilet on the fourth floor of Madrasatul Itqan Li Ulumil Quran in Kutubkhali, Jatrabari.
The child was found with a gamcha wrapped around his neck.
The following day, his father filed a murder case against three teachers — Maulana Qari Anisur Rahman, teacher-in-charge Hafez Maulana Zahirul Islam and Hafez Mohammad Ullah.
According to the case statement, Ziaur Rahman suspects that the accused may have attempted to sexually assault his son or that the child may have witnessed an incident involving them.
He alleged that the three accused, along with four or five unidentified people, killed Mudachchir sometime between 4:15pm and 6:30pm on December 20.
He further alleged that the body was hung from the ventilation of the teachers’ toilet with a gamcha to divert the investigation.
The other two accused have yet to be arrested, according to the father.

item.title: Court orders seizure of ex-railway minister’s 18 plots, 2 cars
item.description:
A Dhaka court has ordered the seizure of 18 plots of land in Comilla, along with two Toyota vehicles owned by former railway minister Md Mujibul Haque, in a corruption case. The court also ordered the freezing of six bank accounts held in his name.
Dhaka Metropolitan Senior Special Judge Md Shahjahan Kabir passed the order on Thursday following an application by Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Assistant Director Papon Kumar Saha.
According to the ACC, Mujibul Haque allegedly abused his power while serving as a public servant, including as railway minister and lawmaker, and, in collusion with others, acquired and possessed Tk7.39 crore in assets beyond his known sources of income through dishonest means.
The ACC filed the case against him under Section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, and Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947.
During the investigation, scrutiny of records found that attempts were being made to transfer or dispose of movable and immovable assets owned by or linked to the accused, the ACC said in its application.
The commission said transferring or disposing of the assets before the case is resolved could cause significant financial loss, prompting it to seek the court’s order to secure the properties.

item.title: Minister Millat’s vehicle fined after driving on wrong side in Dhaka
item.description:
Traffic police stopped a vehicle carrying Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat in Dhaka on Thursday morning after it was allegedly found driving on the wrong side of the road, filing two cases and imposing Tk 6,000 in fines.
The incident took place after 9am when the Range Rover, bearing registration number Dhaka Metro-Gha-18-2125, was traveling toward the Secretariat after passing in front of Kakrail Mosque, according to sources familiar with the incident.
A Traffic Ramna Division official wishing to be anonymous, said the vehicle had violated its lane and was obstructing normal traffic movement. The official said traffic police stopped the vehicle in front of the Secretariat and informed its driver, Arif Hossain, that driving on the wrong side of the road in such a manner was a violation of traffic rules.
The official said the vehicle was carrying a flag and that the minister was inside when traffic police stopped it. A traffic officer on duty subsequently detained the vehicle, and the cases were filed in the presence of senior officials.
Traffic Sergeant Sifat Mahmud, who was on duty at the time, filed the two cases.
The two cases carry fines of Tk 3,000 each, totaling Tk 6,000. One case was filed for creating an obstruction to traffic movement, while the other was for driving the vehicle unsafely.
Speaking to the media about the incident, Sergeant Sifat said: “I could not believe that a case could be filed against a minister’s vehicle. It is a rare incident.”
He said the traffic control room had also been informed about the incident and that the Special Security Force (SSF) had instructed them to take action.
“The driver of the vehicle also admitted to violating traffic rules,” Sifat said.

item.title: Shapla Chattar case: ICT orders Hasina, 29 others to surrender
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal-2 on Thursday ordered 30 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, to surrender before the tribunal by September 16 in a case over the alleged Shapla Chattar massacre during a Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh rally in 2013.
The three-member ICT-2, headed by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, passed the order and directed the authorities concerned to publish advertisements in daily newspapers notifying the accused of the order.
The tribunal also set September 30 for the next hearing in the case.
Ten arrested accused, including former minister Hasanul Haque Inu, writer Shahriar Kabir and former minister Dipu Moni, were produced before the tribunal on Thursday.
However, journalist Farzana Rupa was not brought before the tribunal as she was unwell.
The other accused produced before the tribunal were former state minister for home Shamsul Haque Tuku, former food minister Dr Abdur Razzaque, former minister Abdul Latif Siddiqui, former IGP AKM Shahidul Haque, Major General (retd) Ziaul Ahsan, former DIG Abdul Jalil Mondal and former managing director of Ekattor TV Mozammel Haque Babu.
Earlier, on August 16, 11 accused were scheduled to be produced before the tribunal.
On July 27, ICT-2 took cognizance of the formal charges filed by the prosecution against 41 accused.
The case involves two charges, including the killing of 32 people at Shapla Chattar on May 5, 2013, and the killing of 20 people on May 6 in Siddhirganj, Narayanganj, and other parts of the country.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 986 as three die in 24 hours
item.description:
Three children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Thursday, raising the country’s combined number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 986 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With these, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 887, while confirmed deaths from measles have remained the same at 99.
A total of 964 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 161,148.
Meanwhile, 80 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 19,527.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 141,449 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country, of whom 136,405 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: El Nino could be strongest in decades, UN warns
item.description:
El Nino could be the strongest since records began four decades ago, the United Nations’ climate agency warned Thursday, with the UN chief warning the world is in the “danger zone of extreme weather.”
The naturally-occurring weather phenomenon is set to become “very strong” in the months ahead and is near certain to persist through to February, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said.
El Nino warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns.
“If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began -- so literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades,” WMO chief Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva.
El Nino will peak towards the end of this year -- though its knock-on impacts for the climate will continue well into 2027, said the WMO.
Heat in the oceans releases more slowly into the atmosphere, pushing up global temperatures the following year.
The powerful 2023-24 El Nino contributed to 2024 being the warmest year on record, and “we should not be surprised if this record is broken,” Saulo added.
“El Nino is firmly established and will intensify into a very strong event in the coming months, with big impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns and associated risks of floods, drought and extreme heat,” the WMO said.
El Nino is a natural climate phenomenon and is not caused by climate change.
But scientists expect it will exacerbate the heat of a planet already warming from burning fossil fuels, while amping up weather extremes.
“El Nino is being supersized before our eyes,” said UN chief Antonio Guterres.
“The science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up. Sea surface temperatures are rising, temperatures keep climbing, and the world is in the danger zone of extreme weather.
“The race now is between rising risks and our commitment to take climate action and protect people. We must win that race.”
“This exceptional El Nino... has the potential to deliver a massive blow to communities and economies across the world,” said Saulo.
“We are already seeing disruption and devastation from droughts and floods, and we expect these impacts to increase as El Nino intensifies.”
She put disaster management authorities and climate-sensitive sectors like agriculture, health, energy and water on notice, saying there was “no time to lose” in getting ready.
El Nino typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months.
Conditions oscillate between El Nino and its opposite La Nina, with neutral conditions in between.
“Fueled by exceptionally warm ocean conditions across the tropical Pacific, El Nino is expected to strengthen further during the coming months to a very strong intensity,” the WMO said.
The UN agency classifies El Nino events as weak, moderate, strong or very strong -- meaning it is set to reach the highest level out of four.
The WMO said there was an “exceptionally high likelihood of nearly 100%” that El Nino will continue through to February.
El Nino can reshape weather and climate patterns thousands of kilometers away from the tropical Pacific.
Every El Nino is different, but major events often follow familiar patterns. This includes drought across parts of the Amazon, Indonesia and Australia, disrupted monsoons in India, and shifting rainfall throughout the tropics.
For September-November, WMO forecasts indicate an increased likelihood of above-normal temperatures “across almost all land areas,” alongside rainfall patterns showing a “pronounced and classic atmospheric response to the strong Pacific El Nino,” the UN’s weather and climate agency said.
The index which measures sea surface temperature anomalies in the central eastern equatorial Pacific has strengthened from an average 1.5°C above normal between May and July.
Weekly values between late July and mid-August ranged from around 2.2°C to 2.6°C above average, indicating continued El Nino intensification.
In some areas, subsurface ocean temperatures were more than 8°C above average during July and early August.

item.title: PM greets Hindu community on Janmashtami
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday greeted the members of the Hindu community in Bangladesh and around the world on the occasion of Janmashtami to be celebrated on Friday.
In a message, he urged people of all faiths to play a conscious and responsible role in maintaining social order, brotherhood and communal harmony and remain vigilant against any attempt to disrupt the peaceful atmosphere.
“I urge everyone to be vigilant so that no one can destroy this atmosphere of harmony,” he said.
The prime minister described Janmashtami as a significant religious occasion for Hindus and extended greetings to Hindu brothers and sisters and followers of Sanatan Dharma.
Referring to Hindu scriptures, he said Lord Krishna was born in Mathura on the eighth day of the waning fortnight of the lunar month during the reign of the tyrant King Kansa.
Krishna later ended Kansa’s oppressive rule, upheld righteousness and fought evil, he said.
The prime minister said Krishna’s life and teachings embody humanism, justice, equality and peace, while his ideals of devotion, human welfare and harmony continue to inspire people.
He said people of different religions and beliefs in Bangladesh have been practicing their faiths with mutual respect and harmony from ancient age.
He expressed hope that the ideals of Shri Krishna would further strengthen mutual harmony and brotherhood in the society.
The prime minister wished happiness, peace and prosperity for all on the occasion of Janmashtami.

item.title: Police: Five arrested with weapons over planned Banani robbery
item.description:
Five people have been arrested in Banani while allegedly preparing to commit a robbery, police said.
The arrestees were identified as Md Masud Rana, 29; Md Rajib Hawladar, 30; Hafizul Matbar, 24; Mohammad Shakil Hossain, 24; and Md Badal, 42.
Additional Police Commissioner (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre on Thursday afternoon.
A foreign-made pistol, a magazine, a walkie-talkie, a pair of handcuffs bearing the Bangladesh Police emblem and other items allegedly intended for use in the robbery were recovered from them. Police also seized a Hiace microbus.
Gulshan Division of the Detective Branch received information around 9:30am that a group was preparing to carry out a robbery on Road No 4 in the Banani police station area, said the DMP official.
Acting on the tip-off, a 45-member DB team took position in the area and later conducted a raid in front of Khayer Palace on Road No 4, where the five suspects were arrested.
During the operation, police recovered a foreign-made pistol, a magazine, a walkie-talkie, a pair of handcuffs bearing the Bangladesh Police emblem, a roll of black adhesive tape, a shopping bag and the Hiace microbus.
The DB is interrogating the suspects to determine why they had gathered in the area and to establish details of their alleged robbery plan.
Investigators are also looking into whether the suspects are members of an organized criminal group, the source of the firearm, and whether they have previous criminal records or links to other offenses, police said.
Legal proceedings against the suspects are being initiated at Banani Police Station. Police are also continuing operations to identify and arrest others allegedly involved with the group.

item.title: Dengue: Four more die as 1,252 cases recorded in 24 hours

Since the start of the dengue onslaughts Bangladesh this year witnessed so far 111 deaths while the disease inflicted 39,532.
The dengue last year claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, the dengue claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

Madrasa teacher arrested over rape allegation in Narayanganj
item.description:
Police have arrested a madrasa teacher in Fatullah, Narayanganj, over an allegation of raping a 17-year-old student.
The accused, Md Rafiqul Islam, 28, was arrested from Tahsinul Quran Madrasa in Muslim Nagar on Wednesday after local residents detained him and called the national emergency service 999.
Fatullah Model Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Anwar Hossain confirmed the arrest to Dhaka Tribune on Thursday afternoon.
He said the student’s father filed a case at the police station over the allegation. The student was sent to a hospital for a medical examination, while police have started investigating the case.
According to police, a resident of Muslim Nagar called 999 on Wednesday afternoon and reported that a teacher at the madrasa had allegedly raped a 17-year-old student.
The report prompted local residents to detain and beat the teacher, creating tension in the area. The emergency service subsequently informed Fatullah police station and requested police intervention.
A police team later went to the madrasa and arrested Rafiqul with the help of local residents before taking him to the police station.
Police sources said the student had completed Hifz, or memorization of the Quran, and enrolled at Tahsinul Quran Madrasa about a year ago to further improve his Quran memorization.
According to the allegations, Rafiqul had been sexually abusing the student for about a year by intimidating him.
The latest alleged assault took place on the night of August 31, after which the student fell ill, police sources said.
The student’s mother took him home for treatment. After learning about the alleged assault, she and local residents went to the madrasa and confronted the teacher.
Rafiqul is the son of the late Abdul Mannan of Barunda village under Tongibari police station in Munshiganj. He had been working as a teacher at Tahsinul Quran Madrasa in Muslim Nagar, Fatullah.
The information was provided in a statement issued by the national emergency service 999.

item.title: President urges expatriates to contribute to country’s development
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Thursday called upon Bangladeshi business people living abroad to further contribute to the country’s development by investing their money and making efforts to bring more foreign investment in the country.
The president made the call when a delegation of Bangladeshi expatriates living in the United Kingdom paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban on Thursday afternoon, President’s Press Wing sources said.
Led by UK-based prominent businessman Kamal Uddin, the delegation congratulated Mirza Fakrul on assuming the office of the president.
The president gratefully recalled immense contribution of the expatriates to the movement for establishing democracy and justice in the country through investing their money, labour and intellect, saying “the country and its people would always remember your contribution and role.”
The president also expressed gratitude to the expatriates, noting that their remittances are one of the major driving forces of the country’s economy.
During the meeting, the delegation sought the president’s support to enhance business opportunities and civic facilities for them, including addressing the issue of harassment in the airports. They also urged for ensuring their voting rights in the country.
President Fakhrul Islam said, the government has already started working to resolve these problems and enhance civic facilities for the expatriates.
"Probashi Card has been introduced to ensure comprehensive service facilities and benefits for the expatriates,” he said.
He also urged expat Bangladeshis to invest more in the country, contribute to employment generation, education, healthcare, technology and skill development and other social welfare activities.
The delegation expressed interest in investing in the country.
President’s military secretary and press secretary were present at the meeting.

During the meeting, the two sides held an open and cordial exchange of views on issues of mutual interest and stressed the need to further strengthen the long-standing friendly and historic ties between Bangladesh and Malaysia, according to a press release.

The meeting also discussed in detail Malaysia’s possible role in addressing Bangladesh’s ongoing energy crisis and the issue of Rohingya repatriation.

They expressed hope that cooperation between the two countries will continue to grow in the coming days.
